title: Amazing performance and screen
text:
This has been a great laptop so far. The screen in particular is just awesome -- 1440p resolution, 240hz refresh rate, and bright, vibrant colors. Playing WoW on this is stunning, I've never seen that game look so good. Performance is also excellent, as long as you're plugged into an outlet. It runs Apex Legends at a buttery smooth 120+ fps on ultra graphics settings at 1440p, which is better than my desktop PC (i5-9600K / RTX 2070 Super). I like the design too, it's not garishly "gamer-y" but still has some slick flairs like the glowing ring light on the back.

It does have a few problems. Out of the box, mine had a broken Windows 11 install. The system settings app wouldn't open at all (crashed every time I attempted to launch it) and none of the "easy" fixes I found online worked. I ended up having to download and reinstall Windows 11 entirely, which was annoying but thankfully fixed the problem.

More concerningly, with its factory settings this laptop will run HOT when gaming. The CPU regularly hits 100 degrees C (the CPU's thermal junction max) playing Apex Legends and Overwatch, which is not great for the life of the CPU. I plan to look into undervolting it at some point to help get those temps under better control. Also, as to be expected from any gaming laptop, the fans can get fairly loud when the laptop is under load. Not a problem if you're wearing headphones, but might be bothersome for any other people in the same room.

Overall, this is an easy recommendation if you're in the market for a powerhouse gaming laptop. If the high temps scare you, look into the Ryzen versions of this laptop -- AMD's Ryzen CPUs typically run cooler and are more energy efficient than Intel's.

title: Really great travel laptop
text:
This is a really full featured portable laptop. If you're looking for something powerful and portable, I think it's a great choice.

- Features: While it doesn't have the specs of a gaming laptop, this has a lot of power, especially given how light it is. If you don't want a balanced approach, you can definitely find something that does at least one thing better, of course. A dedicated gaming laptop will be better at running demanding games, obviously. If you're really looking for something to run basic web and word processing apps, you can save some money with a less muscley laptop, and if you're looking to maximize portability and don't need a 15" screen, you can definitely get something lighter and/or with better battery life. Overall, this is really pretty good at all of those things, so it might hit a sweet spot for a lot of people.

- Screen: The 4K OLED screen is crisp and beautiful. Colors and blacks really pop.

- Build: the aluminum case feels sturdy, and the laptop has the basic ports. Power, 1 USB-C, 2 USB-A, HDMI, headphones, and a card reader. It's easy to upgrade ram.

- Performance: this can run most apps and games - the apps look great, and the games are adequate. We're getting 6-8 hours of performance off charger, which is pretty good. Videos look awesome on the OLED screen.

As said, all in all this is pretty nice, and our daughter has announced it's now her primary laptop, because it's great for her needs, feels sturdy, and is easy for her to move from room to room. If you're looking for a high performance, fairly portable laptop with a 15" OLED screen, I think you'll like it a lot.

text:

Guys, this laptop isn't just a gaming laptop. It will run Beat Saber at 144HZ at 100% resolution, no supersampling. You will need to set the game at 2x MSAA anti-aliasing and lower reflection, but after that expect smooth 144HZ with no hiccups. This is before I turned on Turbo Mode.

This can be lowered to 120HZ and you wont have to deal with alot of compromises. Beat Saber plays very well on this RTX2060 powered laptop, making this laptop the ideal entry-level laptop for VR enthusiast.

I mainly bought this laptop as my main streaming/video editing laptop with a side of games and VR Games on the go. My main PC has a Ryzen 5 3600 and a RTX 2070 Super. Of course I'll definitely prefer playing anything on my PC. But this little guy definitely gets the job done when I'm away from home.

title: Great deal on powerful gaming laptop with some limits
text:
Acer has really hit it out of the park with their Helios 300 gaming laptop line, in terms of offering high end gaming laptop specs at a reasonable price. This laptop offers both a high end laptop NVIDIA graphics card (RTX 3060) and a fairly high end 11th generation Intel processor (I7-11800H). They include a 144Hz refresh rate FHD display. They throw in a fast 512Gb NVMe boot drive, a Killer/Intel Ax1650i Ethernet/WiFi system, and a generous array of laptop ports. All at a price that's considerably cheaper than competitors are asking laptops with comparable specs.

If you're looking for specs at the best price, this has what you're looking for. Add to that good quality build, a very efficient fan/vent system, and decent aesthetics, and you may think about ending your search now. Because you won't find a comparable quality system with comparable specs for less.

But there are some downsides. Battery life is pretty poor. You'll get maybe 3.5-4 hours if you put the laptop in Default mode, turn down the brightness, and focus on tasks that don't require the NVIDIA GPU. So, for example, simple video streaming or web surfing. 3.5 hours is not enough for a long plane trip, nor for a take-along laptop for a whole day's classes. And things get a lot worse if you put it into gaming mode (e.g. Turbo). Compared to 10+ hours available with today's road warrior laptops, you can see what you're getting into here. This isn't a gaming laptop that doubles as a do-everything portable. If you need portable and good battery life (and lighter weight--this weighs 5 1/2 pounds), consider something else. This is fine for a trip to the coffee shop for an hour or two.

But if you're a gamer first, you may well be willing to make that trade off.

Beyond the weak battery life, the other significant negative about this laptop is the keyboard. For reasons I don't fathom on a gaming laptop, Acer has chosen to shrink the keyboard on the left side to make room for a dedicated keypad. As a result, I find typing cramped, and find myself frequently hitting the wrong key. The chicklet style keys are also not the most comfortable I've used on a laptop. If you're using this at home, you'll almost certainly want to move to an external keyboard. Which is kind of a shame since the backlit keyboard, with the colored LEDS, IS quite pretty for a laptop keyboard.

Two other so-so components are the Webcam--which only supports HD (1280x720) and isn't all that great, and the built-in speakers. The speakers get the job done, but don't get that loud and are fairly lacking in bottom end. I've heard better laptop speakers, for sure.

Balancing out the weaknesses in battery and keyboard is plenty of easy expandability and upgradability. There are THREE (!!!) mass storage connections in the laptop: Two NVMe connections (one holding the boot drive from the factory), and a place for a third, 2.5" drive. There are two memory slots, one of which holds the 16Gb memory stick for the base configuration. A maximum of 32Gb are supported, if you add a second 16Gb stick. The WiFi card is also easily accessed once the back cover is off, if you decide you want to upgrade the WiFi capabilities in the future. Removing the back cover is straightforward: Remove 11 screws on the bottom, then carefully pry the cover off (there are a few clips around the edges that will release with a careful pull).

Unlike many recent laptops, Acer is pretty generous here with connection ports. You get:

1x Thunderbolt 4 port (USB-C)
1x USB (Type A) 3.2 gen 2 (10 Mb/s)
2x USB (Type A) 3.2 gen 1 (5Mb/s)
1x HDMI
1x Mini-Displayport
1 x Gigabit Ethernet port
1/8" headphone jack

The inclusion of both the latest-and-greatest Thunderbolt 4 port (capable of both 40 Mb/s speeds and supporting up to 2 x 4K/60Hz or 1x 8K/60Hz monitor) is a plus. It's also nice there are three type-A USB ports, all of which are USB 3, and one of which is the faster USB 3.2 gen type. Providing support for both Mini-DisplayPort AND HDMI is icing on the cake.

Power is supplied via a barrel-type power port on the back of the laptop. The power supply is rated for up to 200W. There's no indication that the laptop can be charged through the Thunderbolt port, and there are few generic charger options for 200W in any event.

Value added software included with the laptop includes a copy of the excellent video editing program Cyberlink Powerdirector, the the DTS sound processing application for speakers attached through the 1/8" mini-jack. There's also a control program for the Killer/Intex Ax1650i card.

I ran the popular 3D Mark benchmarking program on the laptop in three modes: Balanced, Extreme, and Turbo. These three modes can be toggled through the Acer/Predator app that comes pre-installed. Turbo mode can also be toggle on/off via a dedicated button the keyboard. Results for the benchmark game Time Spy are (see photos):

Balanced: Graphics Score: 7057, CPU Score: 6403
Extreme: Graphics Score: 7568, CPU Score 7616
Turbo: Graphics Score 7884, CPU Score 7684

The various modes appear to be doing what they should, with the scores improving as you ladder up in overclocking. Given the nominal improvement for Extreme-> Turbo, which also turns on the loud fans permanently, I am not sure that's a power option most people will choose.

Summarizing

Pros
High end discrete graphics card (NVIDIA RTX 3060)
Good cpu (Intel I7-11800H @ 2.30Ghz, 8 cores, 16 thread)
Very generous port assortment, including Thunderbolt 4
144Hz 3ms refresh rate FHD (1920 x 1080) IPS screen, no touch
Fast NVMe 512Gb boot drive (Samsung MZVL2512HCJQ-0080)
Expansion for TWO additional storage devices (1xNVME, 1x 2.5" drive)
Expansion for additional memory stick
Back cover relatively easy to remove to access components
Comes with Cyberlink Powerdirector and DTS software
Offers multiple pre-tuned options for speed/overclock/fan noise
Very pretty backlit keyboard with multi-color LEDs

Cons
Only fair battery life (< 4 hours in nominal use mode, closer to 2 hours in Turbo game mode)
Keyboard squeezed to make way for number pad and a bit uncomfortable/clumsy to use long term
Under stress, fans are very loud
Weak built-in speakers
Mediocre built-in webcam
Only comes with 16Gb of memory, 32Gb would have been preferred
512Gb of storage is fine for productivity apps, but gamers will almost certainly require more for games

Despite the cons, I think this is a lot of laptop for the price, and as long as you can live with the practical need to be on a power source if you're going to do any serious gaming with it, this is probably going to be the most attractive gaming laptop for a lot of people at its price point.

title: Outstanding gaming laptop
text:
If you're looking for the top of the line in gaming laptops, look no further than here.

First, on the look of the laptop itself, it looks really slick, modern, etc. Of course, it is heavier than an every day non gaming laptop, but as far as other comparable gaming laptops, it's actually not too heavy.

Regarding the display, I'm actually very impressed. Of course, the screen is smaller than a monitor, but as far as gaming laptops go, 240HZ is very rare, especially at this price point. If you're not gaming a ton, then the difference between 240HZ and 144HZ isn't huge, and I'd probably say go with the cheaper option. But, if you play a lot and need/like to play on a laptop instead of a desktop/monitor, this is a huge bonus for the sake of your eyes.

As far as battery life goes, it's good, but playing any sort of battery intensive game without sitting at a desk isn't particularly feasible, so I'm always plugged in when I'm playing . But if you're just using it as a normal laptop, then you should be fine using it for extended periods of time without power.

They keyboard on the laptop is very nice for gaming or for normal use. Personally, I prefer to plug in a mechanical keyboard when gaming simply because that's what I'm used to. But, if I don't have one with me, the laptop keyboard actually works pretty well. Also, the trackpad is alright for normal use. Of course, you're not using a trackpad when you're gaming so it doesn't particularly matter for that, but it's a pretty average trackpad overall.

As far as the capacity of the machine, it can run just about any game you need it to. The graphics card is one of the top on the market, and for any common game (Fortnite, Minecraft, COD, etc.) you'll have no problem running those games at basically any settings you want, especially because the cooling mechanism is so good on this computer. Even for more niche games that require a lot more power (for instance Rust), you'll be able to play the game easily without any hiccups or damage to the machine.

Overall, I would 100% recommend this laptop for gaming. For non-gaming, I may look elsewhere. I think there are certain features that are missing from this laptop that are much better for school/work/etc., and you don't need most of the features that come with this laptop. But, if you're looking for a hybrid gaming/work computer, this is certainly an option.

title: A Really Fine Gaming Laptop!
text:
I'm a big gamer so I was very eager to try out this computer. Since anyone can read the computer specifications on the product page, I won't bore you with putting them all down again and I'll just give you my review of the Asus ROG Strix GL502 Gaming Laptop.

1) Its blazing fast - I mean mind-blowingly so for a non-home built computer. I regularly play the MMO Star Wars: The Old Republic and I have to tweak the graphics setting on all three of my computers (a 2012 HP Desktop stock model with upgraded RAM and gaming video card, an 2009 HP laptop that was state of the art gaming at the time of purchase and a recently installed Solid State Drive, and a 2014 Dell Touchscreen Computer which is a decent computer but 100% stock) to a varying degree. However, I had no such issues with the Asus Gaming Laptop. I immediately installed SWTOR, turned the graphics setting to the craziest, highest settings that I could (some that I'd never even considered tweaking even on my desktop computer) and the laptop didn't even blink. The movement and game play action was so fast and I didn't experience any of the jittering or hesitation that I'd seen on my other computers when the graphics were set too high.

2) The laptop screen is crystal clear and has truly beautiful graphics display. Although the screen is a little on the small side for me, even my HP laptop has a 17" screen and both my desktop and touchscreen have 30" screens, the display is so perfect that I've found myself not caring. I've recently gotten into Mass Effect 2 again on Steam and I was somewhat surprised when I didn't feel like the screen was cramped or too small for me to play the game adequately. I didn't measure that angle exactly, but I could tell that the monitor has a great viewing angle as my daughter could stand comfortably to one side while watching me play games.

3) This is only peripherally about the computer, but since it affects the use of the computer I got to say it - Windows 10 sucks. I hate how Microsoft tries to turn the laptop into a tablet by installing all kinds of apps that I then have to turn around and uninstall. I hate that it has so many bugs that I need to go into the Bios to get the number pad to work at login and I can't install a printer because it takes down the WiFi capability of the laptop. And this is just off the top of my head. Windows 10 is terrible. Thankfully it doesn't seem to affect my game play as I was able to install and properly use Steam and my MMO's.

4) As I said, my HP laptop has a pretty big keyboard (essentially the same size as a normal keyboard), so it took me a little bit of time to get used to the smaller size of the Asus keyboard. However, it was slightly bigger than my work laptop so I didn't really mind it all that much. I would have liked the ability to shut off the touchpad since I use a wireless gaming mouse as I sometimes accidentally swipe across it while playing (which is kind of annoying).

5) Despite the high-powered capabilities of the Asus gaming laptop, it is super slim and very light. Some of this has to do with its 100% plastic construction, but despite this the laptop appears to be very strong and sturdy (although I clearly didn't drop-test it).

6) The fan and venting on the computer is honestly pretty darn good. Although the computer gets kind of warm during heavy game play, it is nowhere near as hot as my other laptop gets. Considering how thin and light the laptop is, I was very impressed at the laptop's ability to dissipate heat.

7) Although I typically use my gaming headset microphone, when I tested out the on-board microphone I had no issues with it clearly picking up my speech on my team-speak application.

Overall, despite my complete revulsion of Windows 10, I really can't say anything bad about the Asus ROG Strix GL502 Gaming Laptop and in fact I am overjoyed at its gaming speed. It performs far better than I could have even hoped! As far as cost goes, my high-end HP laptop cost me $3300 and my upgraded HP desktop cost $2200, so $1449.99 for this SWEET thing is a bargain in my book. Two thumps WAY UP on the Asus ROG Strix GL502 Gaming Laptop

title: I love this laptop! (Review Updated)
text:
Update to the below review! I figured out that by default the integrated graphics card is used, so my comments below about game performance were with the integrated graphics. Doh! Now this is a bit of a pain but you must open the nvidia control panel and pick out/assign your games to use the Nvidia graphics card. There's nothing automatic about this so you have to do it or it uses the internal card.

Now that I have the games using the nvidia, I can play bf4 and fallout 4 both at 4k just fine and they look amazing.

**Original review below***

This is a great laptop for professionals or gamers that travel. Another review said it was not good for gaming and I'm going to have to disagree with that. Can you play games @ ultra quality with 4k? Nope. But are most modern games playable at decent resolutions? Absolutely.

* It's fast. Very fast. I ran geekbench and it beat out every other processor in the house including an 8700k and a 5960x which are beasts.

* The fingerprint sensor is in the power button and it's pretty nice. It is sensitive enough and quick. Breeze to use.
* Battery life is great, I was able to play a game for several hours easily.
* The screen is absolutely beautiful. Large with nice bright colors and a deep black.
* It's very stylish, looks and feels expensive. Fit and finish is top notch.

Only a couple of downsides to the laptop

* The hard drive is 256gb which is a little small for the power of this laptop and the fact that you can play real games. If I was buying one I would opt for the 512gb option.

title: Killer specs for gaming yet stealthy for business use
text:
If you are reading this, you likely already know what incredible specs this laptop has, but let me summarize them:

12th Generation Intel Core i9-12900H processor, the latest NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti, 16" WQXGA (2560 x 1600) DCI-P3 100% IPS LED-backlit NVIDIA G-SYNC display, maxed out with 32GB LPDDR5 memory, and a 1TB PCIe Gen 4x4 SSD.

It was a true pleasure to review this unit. This is my second day with it, so I wanted to write this while my first impressions were fresh. It came well protected and in classy packaging, much like you would expect from an Apple product. It has been a while since I've worked with an Acer product, and my expectations have certainly changed for the better after using this one. The construction quality and attention to details is comparable to the best. For that matter if you are familiar with the weight, size and feel of a 15" MacBook Pro you would swear the designers at Acer's intent was to make this blend in with a board room filled with those, and they certainly succeeded. In other words, well built, solid, yet sexy in an understated way. If the RGB backlighting is set for white and solid, even the keyboard has the same look and feel. I've included some side by side shots so you might see what I'm referring too. Weight wise I could not tell the difference, but after placed them both on a kitchen scale (slightly off center, so less than accurate) I could see the Acer was roughly 10 ounces heavier, BUT the comparison stops there. This machine has the power and muscle to play games like no Mac laptop could. I can only assume that Acer's goal was for it to look nothing like a gaming laptops, so it can be used for work and play. They certainly succeeded; it performs like the very best gaming machines currently being produced, and not surprisingly considering the cost and specs. The only way you could gain more gaming performance would be to move to a desktop; though then you would be giving up mobility, and likely spend more.

If you don't plan to use this in the work place, it comes down to personal taste, but you may still like its understated look. Without tearing it apart I can not be sure, but the bottom case and top layer have the look and feel of aluminum (if it is coated plastic, then they did a fantastic job). Only the bezel around the screen has the appearance of plastic, yet is finished to match the rest, so still looks good. The speakers sound great (better than any laptop I've used), and the track pad is large and responsive with a fingerprint reader in the top left corner that works well for logging into and waking up the machine free from passwords. The number of ports and placement seem good for my needs though I wish the power port had some sort of quick disconnect like Apple's do. Honestly that is the only change I would have liked, and I'm unaware of any of the other Window's gaming laptops having that feature, so I will just need to be careful with that.

Overall this laptop is perfect. Now off to play some StarCraft II at full resolution with all settings maxed out. :). If I make any new discoveries in the coming weeks, I'll be back to provide an update.

title: A fast and capable Windows 10 desktop replacement laptop
text:
#### Appearance, materials, etc.

This is a standard laptop with a touchscreen. Unlike some Windows 10 laptops, it does not have a 180º hinge that flips the screen back to “presentation mode” or make it turn into a tablet.

In terms of overall construction, it is a black plastic laptop encased in silver anodized aluminum. It is slightly wedge shaped, and strives to look thinner than it actually is.

#### Portability

I put this laptop in the “desktop replacement” class. Despite the extra small bezels around its screen, it appears to have been optimized for performance rather than for size and weight. The Dell’s length and width exactly match those of my 2013 15” MacBook Pro. Its height (on the hinge end), when closed, is almost a quarter inch more than the old MacBook Pro, too. It is much heavier than the MacBook Pro, as well. I am pretty sensitive to size and weight when putting laptops in my bag, but the way I use this laptop—around the house—they do not matter that much.

#### Keyboard and track pad

The parts of the laptop that you will touch all the time feel very good.

The keyboard and trackpad feel good to the touch and work with great accuracy on Windows 10. Trackpads on Windows PCs traditionally lagged behind Apple MacBook trackpads in terms of quality, but I think the Dell’s trackpad is great. It is not oversized, like the newer Apple laptops, or crowded with hardware buttons, like on Lenovo Yoga laptops, or weirdly textured, like on the HP Satellite.

The keyboard is really good. It has good travel, properly sized keys, a sensible layout, And a T-shaped arrow cluster. There is far greater travel than the current generation of MacBook Pros, and about the same as the Lenova Yoga I use for work every day. I think I type more accurately on the Yoga, but I think I just need more time to get used to the key feel and key travel on the Dell. One minor nit about the keyboard: the bumps or ridges on the bottom of the F and K keys are very hard to feel, which makes it harder than I would like to get my fingers into typing position without looking at the keyboard.

The area around the keyboard is black, soft-touch plastic. It feels nice, and never felt cold (like aluminum cases do) or hot (when the fans blow). Its edges are rolled off, ever so slightly, so typing is always a comfortable experience. I absolutely hated the Intel sticker that was on it, but, to my surprise, it peeled off easily and left no residue behind.

The track pad reminds me of MacBook Pro trackpads from about 5-6 years ago, before they got comically large. It is a normal-sized, clicky trackpad with no physical buttons and a pleasantly smooth surface. It worked perfectly for accurate pointing and multi-finger gestures. It is the best trackpad of all my Windows laptops.

The power button, which sits to the right of the keyboard, contains a fingerprint sensor, which works very much like Touch ID does on an (older) iPhone or iPad. In my experience, setting up and using the sensor was quick and easy. Windows 10 allows you to log in with a fingerprint, which is fast and worked flawlessly.

#### The screen

The 4K, 15.6” LCD touch-enabled display is gorgeous. Everything about it is good. Colors pop on the default Windows wallpaper, but look accurate to me on my photos. The 4K resolution works very well at this screen size: text is very sharp. Screen brightness is fantastic, too. Many Windows laptops I have used have rather dim screens, which make Them almost impossible to use outside (even in shade) or near sunny windows (at the local coffeeshop, say). The Dell’s screen can get very, very bright, which provides far greater flexibility and visibility than I expected. The screen has an integrated touch panel, which I don't use all the time, but I absolutely love, because it makes Windows 10 a little easier to use.

#### Ports

There is a mishmash of ports on each side, which make it versatile for all kinds of uses. On the left, you have a power port, USB 3 Type A, HDMI, USB C, and a headphone/microphone jack. On the right you have another USB 3 Type A port and an SD card reader. While I welcome these various ports (especially the SD card reader), if you are all-in on USB-C, you may be disappointed. The single USB-C port is the best option for a monitor cable (at least for my monitor, which does not support 4K/60 over HDMI, but does over DisplayPort or USB-C). The USB Type A ports are perfect for plugging in a mouse and keyboard, without requiring a hub or an adapter.

#### Charging

The included power adapter is not USB-C. It is a huge brick with a long, light-up cable that has a circular plug. I did some online research which led me to believe that the USB-C port cannot be used for charging unless your charger pushes at least 60 watts. That means that you can’t trickle-charge your laptop with something smaller, like a tablet or smartphone charger. My ChromeBook came with a 45-watt charger, which I thought was standard for modern laptops, so a 60-watt charger seems pretty powerful to me. You absolutely do not need to use USB-C charging to use this laptop, but it is good to know what you can and cannot do.

#### Performance

Overall, this computer is fast. It is easily the fastest Windows laptop I have ever used, though my nearest point of comparison is a 2-year-old Lenovo Yoga Core i5 system, which is not a fair comparison point. I use it mainly for programming: Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, SQL Server Express, etc. Those heavyweight applications launch pretty fast. Compile times are snappy, and the computer (with 16 GB or RAM) does not get bogged down or resource starved throughout the day.

I have not stressed it too much with my normal computing activities. The fan does come on sometimes, and the fan exhaust goes straight down through rather large vents on the bottom of the case. This is only a problem if you are litterally using this computer on your lap. If it is on a table top, little feet on the bottom of the case prop it up so that the exhaust has somewhere to go. If you use a machine on your bed, or over a blanket that would plug up the exhaust holes, you might want to reconsider that before buying this machine, or look to a different laptop that vents out the back.

I have seem YouTube videos that claim that this laptop’s Core i9 variant runs hot and throttles, which would make the Core i7 model the sweet spot for price-to-performance ratio.

#### Problems

The only problems I have with this machine are Windows 10-related, rather than hardware-related.

My first day with it was, in a large part, wasted on software updates from Microsoft, Dell, and other third parties who have software pre-installed. Also, after running through a couple update-and-reboot cycles, Windows 10 told me that it was not activated. I had to click the “Troubleshoot” button in Windows activation settings to fix it. It is the sort of thing that should not happen, but fortunately it did not cause me much downtime.

Waking the computer up is also problematic. Most of the time, it takes a few presses of the power button to wake up Windows. Once Windows wakes, everything is fine.

#### Overall impressions

Overall, this is a very capable machine for software development. I particularly like the bright, sharp screen and the zippy Core i7 processor. Due to its overall size and weight, I consider it a desktop replacement, rather than an ultraportable, laptop.

In reality I often get about 130-150 on ultra high graphics settings of the (older, processor-bound) games I play. My pinball scores skyrocketed with the higher FPS. I get more clutch kills / heals in League of Legends. Frames win Games.

I played Control to put it through its paces, and it held up extremely well. Control uses Ray-tracing and the difference between rtx on and rtx off is huge, but at the time of writing not very many games support it yet.

To me, this was the sweet spot of value. I wanted a 3080 but the prices were ridiculous. My 1060, 7th gen intel chip wasn't getting great frame rates on high graphics settings in modern games.

title: Excellent PC overall, gaming included
text:
Nothing much to say, really. My main purpose reviewing is telling you about the gotchas in video for this PC. Overall, though, it is absolutely excellent. It is utra quiet even with the fans running at high speed. It does get hot, but no performance issues.

What I learned about video setup: There are three display ports in this PC:

1. Mini DisplayPort v1.4.
2. HDMI port v2.1.
3. Thunderbolt port v4 (USB-C).

All display ports are capable of 4K @60Hz at least. I run my PC connected to 2 LG UltraFine 31.5in monitors at that resolution and refresh rate. However, the DisplayPort function embedded in the Thunderbolt v4 port is run by the integrated Intel HD graphics card, NOT the nVidia RTX3060 card. This is VERY IMPORTANT for gaming: The Intel integrated graphics card will NOT support DirectX 12 Ultimate.

On the other hand, displays connected through ports 1 or 2 above will be un by the nVidia RTX3060 card that does support DirectX 12 Ultimate. The difference is night and day. True, I am not loading the most hardcore games ever, but still. So you get a frame of reference, my main 2 games are Age of Empires II DE and Age of Empires IV. I run both in full desktop mode, meaning the 2 monitors treated as one big monitor. AoE II DE reports consistent FPS of 60 (I have V-Sync on, which limits FPS to that of the monitor's refresh rate) with all graphics settings on. AoE IV does not seem to have a way to show the FPS, but it does run super smoothly.

So there. Enjoy this super high end PC at a super low price. Oh, and you MUST use quality 8K-graded cables. FYI, the HDMI cables that shipped with my LG monitors are garbage. Get Vanky or some other reputable 8K cables.

title: Initial Impressions are Excellent
text:
I've only had the laptop for a day, but my initial impressions are excellent. I was able to pick one up from Amazon Warehouse Deals for a fantastic deal (less than $500 before tax) that I just couldn't pass up. It came repackaged with just the laptop and the charger in a plain box, wrapped well in inflatable packing material. It booted up right away and I was surprised to see that there was a 100% fresh copy of Windows 10 installed. No manufacturer software or drivers at all. This was a refreshing alternative to the bloatware that normally comes bundled with most laptops, but it did mean that I needed to seek out certain software on my own to enable all of the machine's features.

I bought it mostly for gaming in bed, so I could pass my existing HP laptop with a GTX 940m on to my son. So far I've only played a few hours of Civ VI with the latest expansion, but it has been fantastic. At 1080p and medium settings it maintained a solid 60FPS with VSYNC the entire time. I ran the built-in benchmarks and all of them performed similarly, so I would expect even late-game performance to be perfectly acceptable. Thermal performance was good. I checked CPU and GPU temperatures a few times during gameplay and they were maintaining around 75C, which is much cooler than a lot of laptops. The fans did stay pretty loud throughout, however, so if you're sensitive to fan noise then this may not be the model for you.

Hardware-wise, everything looks solid. There is a bit of flex in the plastic chassis but it's the kind that you have to go out of your way to find. Port selection is excellent, which is refreshing given how minimalist many other modern laptops are. I was a bit wary about the combination of a fairly slow HDD and the 16GB Intel Optane module, but it actually does seem to perform pretty well. It's definitely not as fast as a good SSD, but it really isn't bad. It's an acceptable solution at this price and the process of swapping in an SSD or M.2 drive would be a simple one, if you desired more performance.

One thing that other reviews of the GV62 8RD harped on was the screen. It's a 1080p IPS, but it really isn't a top performer. Colors are pretty lifeless and there isn't a lot of pop. However, I'm not a huge stickler for this, and I didn't feel as thought it detracted from my experience much at all. If you plan on doing intensive graphics work where color matters, I'd definitely look elsewhere.

Overall I'm happy with my purchase. Time will tell as to how it holds up, but I'm comfortable giving it 5 stars for now.

title: Good for gaming, not great for basic everyday stuff
text:
UPDATE: Happy to say this laptop works flawlessly with Oculus Rift! (Once you update your graphics card drivers.)

Keep in mind you'll only be able to plug in two sensors unless you get something to give you extra USB ports, but otherwise I was very impressed.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Before I get into the details, I want to note - because this laptop is primarily made for Gaming, I'm giving it 3 stars. If I intended to use this for work or other computer tasks on a regular basis, my rating would be lower.

-GAMING-
When it comes to gaming, so far my experience has been quite positive. That said, I was really disappointed when I realized how quickly this laptop gets uncomfortably hot. Given that it's a LAPtop, I feel it's fair to expect that it be usable without getting unreasonably hot while using it on your lap.

However, I think at least part of this problem is related to how quickly the computer gets overwhelmed. In fact, even during menial tasks like browsing the web or even using the file explorer, the fan will come on because the computer is so overwhelmed. That's something I've never experienced with my main computer unless I have multiple windows with several tabs open that I haven't closed out for a few days, along with a few other applications that have also been left running for a while.

Needless to say, for a computer whose main purpose is performance, I was shocked at how easily I could get it to a state where it was overwhelmed. And yet somehow despite how overwhelmed and hot it gets, it still manages to perform really well when you’re gaming on it. Just don’t play with it on your lap without something to protect your legs! (I may be a little repetitive on this point, but when they brag “an outstanding dual-fan cooling system”… I think you deserve to know it’s not going to protect you!)

Graphically, games look beautiful, and that's definitely one of the best things about this laptop. However, the fan runs so loud when you're doing anything that you'd better have some good headphones so you can still hear the sound over the fan. Given that they say “Experience faster load times and a quieter system”, I have to wonder what they think “quieter” means.

-PHYSICAL DESIGN-
This computer is about as attractive as I’d expect for the brand that made it, which is not very attractive. That said it is on the nicer side out of the computers they make.

It's quite heavy, so I suppose making the body out of plastic is one way to avoid adding to that weight further. However, the plastic is extremely concerning if the laptop were ever to fall even a couple of feet. While I'm extremely careful and don't expect this to happen, especially to a 17 lb. laptop, I have to wonder exactly what the product designers were thinking. "Ah yes, let's make it a 'laptop' so it's portable... but an inch thick with a 17" screen so that that no one can actually find a case for it. Then let's give it a plastic casing so if anyone is foolish enough to transport it without protection, they are incredibly nervous about it."

It just doesn't make sense to me! Maybe there's something I'm missing here as my gaming is usually more focused on consoles, both ones connected to the TV and handheld consoles. That said, for a computer that costs over $1,000, it's concerning to me that there doesn't seem to be a safe way to transport it, despite it being a laptop. I just don't see what the benefit is if you can't feel confident bringing it with you somewhere.

On to my next point, which is... stickers. Why are there stickers on such an expensive product? I know this has been a thing for a long time on PCs, but why? And perhaps more importantly, why are they so hard to take off and why do they live so much sticky residue behind?

The keyboard is really nice and probably the one redeeming feature of the physical design. It feels good to type on and the fact that it can light up different colors is fun. Sadly when trying to use the built in software to adjust the colors so I could have multiple colors at once (more like a rainbow), I couldn’t find any way to get the colors to be as vibrant as the basic default red, blue, and green. Instead they look pale and washed out no matter how much I move around the color wheel.

The trackpad is unfortunately way too easy to hit accidentally and I’ve been looking for a way to disable it completely as it’s really frustrating how in the way it is. I also find it awkward the way it’s positioning off-center, especially because I’m used to laptops with the track pad in the middle where I have space for both hands to comfortably rest while still being able to access the whole keyboard easily.

The area around the keyboard and trackpad also picks up the oils from your skin very quickly so you end up with shiny smudges all over it. Pity since otherwise it would look pretty nice.

Overall it's not the ugliest laptop I've ever seen, but it's not something I'd show off to anyone. And that's saying something given that we've had sleek, beautiful computers publicly available for quite some time now. The only conclusion I can come to is that this brand just doesn't care about design.

-GENERAL USER INTERFACE AND EXPERIENCE-
Having grown up with computers made by this particular brand, I was surprised to see just how many things *haven't* changed in the last 20 years. For example, some of the screens I saw while getting the computer set up for the first time could easily have been designed 20 years ago, and in reality, some of them probably haven't changed in that time as far as their design goes. Rough, pixelated blue and black was not something I expected to ever see on a new computer at this point in my life!

Perhaps more disappointing somehow was how ugly the set-up screens were and how even the default background for the desktop ended up looking obviously pixelated in areas where there are gradients. For a high-end computer that's meant for gaming, I would expect the user interface to at least seem like it's trying to look like it was designed in the last ten years?

In using the computer for everyday tasks, I've had random things pop up at me that I did nothing to trigger, as well as fun little error that come out of nowhere even when all I'm doing is browsing the internet.

Recently I was in the middle of something and the computer started updating itself out of nowhere and didn't give me the option to opt out of it. I'm sure there's a setting somewhere that turns on automatic updates, but to have no chance to prevent my computer from being taken over for nearly an hour when I was working on something is incredibly frustrating to say the least.

Right after setting up the laptop, I went to run the updates that were recommended. Everything was downloaded, it restarted, took a while to get through it, and then I saw a screen pop up with a nature-y background, which promptly disappeared. Then the screen went black and the fan was running really loudly. I sat there for 15 minutes with the screen black and the fan running wondering whether I should be concerned. Eventually I pressed something (had already tried moving the mouse and no luck) and the login screen popped up. After a while I discovered that the login screen doesn't show up automatically. You have to do something to get it to appear. And maybe this is just me, but as someone who hasn't used Windows 10 before, it would have been really nice to have some kind of guidance on how the login screen worked the first time I used it so I wasn't sitting there wondering if my brand new laptop was broken.

In general, this laptop just… seems to have a lot of problems? Both in poorly designed user interface and in actual errors and it not running well at times. I find this pretty concerning given the price and the fact that it’s brand new. I would expect some odd issues here and there maybe 5-8 years down the road, but practically out of the box with hardly anything installed? I expected better.

Also, how is it that in 2019 it’s a several steps long process to take a screenshot that’s not just the whole screen? Instead of having a built-in way to do this, you have to use the ancient “Print Screen” function and then open up an editor to crop the image. This is a huge pain if you ever want or need to take screenshots that are more focused rather than your entire screen.

-CAMERA AND AUDIO-
If you're hoping to use this for any kind of online meeting, please just go look for another computer. The webcam quality is downright awful and the speaker feeds back directly into the microphone because of its placement. Just... don't.

Also, the sound from the speaker in general is just… meh? Things sound kind of flat like there’s no dimension to them.

I’m honestly not a sound person at all, so I can’t say much more. The speaker is just not impressive.

-PORTS-
I really appreciate that this laptop has an ethernet port, an HDMI port, 1 USB port on the left, 1 on the back, and 1 on the right. Dividing up the USB ports in particular is really handy.

There’s also your basic headphone jack, a security lock spot, a DisplayPort, and an SD card slot.

-BATTERY-
This battery is pretty poor for a laptop. As mentioned above, it doesn’t seem to actually be intended to be very portable (except maybe from room to room at home). I suppose if you accept that, it’s fair to assume you can plan on having this plugged in basically all the time, particularly if you’re planning on actually using it for gaming. I believe it lasts around 4 hours with basic computing tasks like browsing the web. My guess is that it’s more like two when I’m gaming.

-THE INSIDES-
I know some people mentioned getting the G5 instead of the G7 in the reviews here. I can confirm that I did get the 17” inch screen, the 16GB of RAM, the i7 processor, and the 512GB hard drive promised(well, 476GB after everything that was pre-installed).

-VR COMPATIBILITY-
I plan to test it with an Oculus Rift soon and plan to update here when I have the chance to do that. From what I can tell, the specs should be high enough. I recently ran the Vive and Oculus test software to make sure it , it's just a matter of which Graphics card is physically set up in the spot that can be accessed by the VR headset? (I'm sure there's a better way of explaining that! But that's my rough understanding of how it works.)

1) Build - I really like the magnesium/aluminum materials that ASUS used in the build of the machine. When you're doing basic tasks such as watching YouTube, working in Excel, checking emails, etc, the G14 is cool to the touch. I also enjoy the way the monitor's hinges lift the laptop off the desk to allow for better airflow. The keyboard feels pretty standard, but definitely one of the better keyboards I've tested on a laptop.

2) Gaming performance - My game of choice is Call of Duty: Modern Warfare. When putting the G14 through a few hours of play, I really enjoyed it. The G14 is able to push out 95-120fps in multiplayer mode and between 90-110 fps in Battle Royal (Warzone). For a laptop this size, I think that is quite impressive. I'm sure I could get more fps if I turned on "Turbo" mode instead of "Performance" mode, but I want the laptop to last awhile so I'm okay with the performance I was getting. My GPU temps never went above 80C.

3) Speakers - These are definitely the best speakers I've tested on a windows laptop.

CONS:

1) Speakers - Yes, I know I said the speakers were a PRO, but they are also a CON. Although they are best speakers I've tested on a windows laptop, the Macbook Pro's speakers provide a better listening experience. This might be important to you if you are a content creator/video editor/someone who just likes better sound from laptop speakers.

2) ASUS Armory Crate - I actually enjoy using the Armory Crate, but I think those who aren't as familiar with tech performance settings might be afraid to use it. It is throwing a lot at you at once. I like being able to see all the technical details about my performance setting, but I do think the way the information is presented could have been better. The layout of Acer's PredatorSense is an example of an easy to read performance center.

3) Price - I see this product retailing for $1,449 + for the version I have here on Amazon. My advice would be to wait until you see the price discounted on Best Buy's site. I was able to get mine for $1,149.00. If it's not on sell today, keep checking, because they keep dropping the price every few weeks.

TLDR; Great laptop. Amazing performance with good thermals. Get it on Best buy for $300+ cheaper.

text:
This laptop is going send me back to the kid’s table on holidays. I had moved away from gaming because, well, I was told it was time for me to grow up. After a couple of weeks tinkering with this offering, she is perfectly welcome to remain the only adult in this relationship.

Personally, this laptop is basically a new desktop for me as I Immediately hooked up a 7 port hub for the use of a gaming mouse, mechanical keyboard, and my favorite base station resident wireless headphones before I began the process of removing ‘nopeware,’ of which there is a healthy supply. You’re going to want a set of quality headphones because the built in speakers are unremarkable.

Some users may elect to do a clean install but I can’t help myself but to look to see if there’s something I might find interesting or helpful and admittedly, there were a couple of things like the ASU Gift Box that did suggest a couple of apps I thought I might try out…then I deleted it. Many users may also want to immediately install some monitoring utilities to stay apprised of temperature levels and other performance issues.

At this point, download is obviously the most accessible alternative for installation because the GL502VT lacks an optical drive so purchase of an external drive is on the list as well as a higher powered cooling pad because after about an hour of playing DOOM the back panel would have been far too hot to sit on my lap. I haven’t tried adjusting power options as I also haven’t encountered any performance problems and as mentioned, it won’t be long before another cooling option is in place.

As noted in the product page description this Intel Quad-Core i7-6700HQ 2.6 GHz (Turbo to 3.5 GHz) laptop is equipped with Windows 10, Wi-Fi 802.11 AC, HD Webcam, Bluetooth 4.1, 16GB DDR4 (one removable 8GB chip) which is also the upward max capacity for this build, 128GB SSD boot drive, 1TB 7200rpm HDD, NVIDIA GTX 970M graphics card with 6GB VRAM, 15.6” FHD IPS display and Hyper Cool Duo-Copper cooling system for CPU/GPU. Peripherals and accessories can be accommodated via 3 USB 3.0 ports, 1 USB3.1 Type C (gen 1) port, HDMI port, mini display port Ethernet jack, SD card reader and combo headphone/microphone jack.

Boot time from the 128GB SSD is blazing fast however with the smallish capacity, it doesn’t take long to run out of space so you’re pretty much obliged to place the majority of games, music/ video files, and productivity products on the 1TB HDD. It hasn’t been a performance problem at all thus far. I haven’t noticed any hints of latency in playing graphic intensive games. I don’t intend to adjust overclocking either as I find turbo boost works well for me. The display on this unit is outstanding, viewable without distortion from angled positions and can be optimised for applications and most popular games via the NVIDIA GeForce utility. While in operation with the battery (which is not installed with the idea of user replacement), about 5 hrs of use can be anticipated for generalized activity (web search, productivity apps, etc.), but under heavier game play, I wouldn't plan on using the laptop for more than somewhere between 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

Aesthetically, I wasn’t a fan of the illuminated orange accents on the cover of the lid but it didn’t take long for that effect to become a superfluous concern. The black brushed aluminum lid also has a minor degree of mushiness if pressed on but overall seems sturdy. The keyboard also features aluminum plating with an orange-accented backlit tactile responsive chiclet keyboard. I’m also not much of a user of the touch pad on this or any other laptop so beyond observing it seems highly responsive and not nearly as flexible as what I have experienced with units like the Toshiba L55, I can’t comment on actual efficiency.

title: Good Overall Device. Would Buy Again.
text:
To begin with, I didn't purchase this device on Amazon (Ebay one this time), but figured this was a good place to share my thoughts about this device since it is generally my first stop when shopping.

Let’s start with aesthetics. This laptop is beautiful. By far the nicest looking laptop I’ve ever owned. It doesn't look like a gaming laptop. The bezels are thin, it’s low profile, and the fan vents aren’t exaggerated like some other gaming type laptops.

With regards to weight, it's a bit heavy, but not too bad. I’d say it feels like a quality sturdy product rather than a heavy one. The power brick is quite large in area, but pretty slim. It is a bit heavy, but not too bad.

Panel

The screen is amazing. The colors are vibrant, and the blacks are deep, as you would expect with an OLED panel. I had a hard time deciding between this panel and the 1080P high refresh rate panel. I figured that I would use this more for editing video / photos and also watching videos.

One issue you should be aware of is the color calibration. Basically, if apps aren’t able to use your color space or a wide gamut, the content will appear over saturated. This is actually a major issue. Apps that are over saturated, to name a few, are DaVinci Resolve (couldn’t find setting in app), Windows Photos, Steam (in game settings may offer wide gamut), etc. Luckily Capture One seems to work fine. I don’t use Adobe products, so I can’t comment on those.

If this panel is going to be your primary or only panel for color related work, make sure you know how to get accurate colors in your application of choice. This has been a bit of an issue for me. Luckily I have another monitor where I can see an estimate of what a final export will look like.

Keyboard

The keyboard does take some getting used to (and is a bit of a fingerprint magnet), but I can type pretty quickly on it. I’ve heard some complaints about the QWERTY portion being off center, but that has not bother me. That’s how my desktop keyboard seems to be as well, so not a big deal in my book.

The keys are tactile and feel good when you’re typing. The RGB back lighting is nice, particularly at night. I’ve turned it off for now, which can be done using the FN key and the space bar. The main issue I’ve had is hitting the numlock button when trying to backspace. I am getting used to this though.

The arrow keys don’t feel natural to reach for. They seem a touch too far to the left. I have to look at them to use them.

10 Key Number Pad

Having a number pad is nice as well. The only issue I have with this is the placement of the 0 key. I seem to hit the right arrow every time I try to enter 0. I’d also say, don’t expect to be as fast with this 10 key as you would be on a regular keyboard. I can’t pinpoint why, but I seem to have to look at it when entering data. Still, I’d rather have it than not have it.

Touch Pad

The touchpad isn’t great, and I’d suggest sticking with a mouse. For me, this is true for most laptops. I’ve had a two major issues with this touchpad.

First, when I’m typing, my left palm slightly touches the touchpad and often moves my cursor while I’m typing. since I’m using an external mouse, I set the touchpad to turn off when a mouse is plugged in.

Second, when clicking on the pad, it is very common to get a right click instead of a left click. This mostly happens when trying to hold left click to select text.

On the side of the touchpad is a fingerprint scanner, which works amazingly well. Seems faster than the one on my Pixel 2.

Speakers

There’s nothing to write home about regarding these speakers. They are on the top of the keyboard (as shown above) and sound okay. Serious users will prefer a headset or external speakers. However, for casual media consumption, they are fine.

Webcam

The webcam here is fine. It’s nice because there is a cover you can slide closed (good for those paranoid types such as myself). It’s positioned at the top of the keyboard and does point up at you, so you will have that awkward view. Since I don’t use this much, I prefer it here as opposed to the top of the display.

Killer Wi-Fi

I’ve had some issues with the Killer Wi-Fi, which for the most part, I was able to troubleshoot with some extensive web searching and trial and error. One issue was that the Gigabyte laptop would disconnect from the internet about every 2 minutes. It also caused all my devices to disconnect including a laptop, desktop, and two android devices. Turns out that my Wi-Fi router has a single channel of 2.4 GHZ. I hooked up another router that was dual band 2.4 GHZ and 5 GHZ and this fixed the main issue.

Prior to this, I did uninstall all Killer applications and installed the drivers only, which you can find on the Killer site. This didn’t help, but one less piece of poor software is good. I still get some random disconnects where the troubleshooter mentions a bad gateway. I think I’ll replace this card with an Intel one at some point.

Manufactures, please read all the complaints online about the Killer Wi-Fi cards and stop using them. These things are awful!

Ports

To sum up the ports, simply amazing. In my opinion, you have all that you’ll ever need.

USB 3.1 Gen 1: #3
Display Port 1.4 / USB 3.1 (Type C): #1
Thunderbolt 3 / Type C: #1
HDMI 2.0: #1
SD Card Reader: #1
Ethernet (RJ 45): #1
Combo Audio Jack: #1

Bloatware

Bloatware hasn’t been intrusive, and I didn’t find much of it. There are some Gigabyte applications, but they haven’t caused any problems. It wasn’t enough to do a clean Windows install which some people using previous generations have suggested to do. The only items I uninstalled were Spotify and some Candy Crush games (gross).

Performance

I’ve done quite a bit of work and testing using this laptop with my findings listed below. Hopefully the sectioning of the content helps you locate performance characteristics for your use case. Keep in mind, I am not a professional, just an Average Joe fiddling around with cool free applications!

Power

With regular use such as word processing, spreadsheet work, YouTube and web browsing I got about 5 hours at the default unplugged brightness setting of 29, which is pretty low. Given the quality of the panel, I didn’t feel like I needed full brightness for the activities I was conducting.

While gaming at full brightness, you will be lucky to get one hour from a charge. I played Sunset Overdrive at 4K and hit 10% battery power after an hour. It wasn’t too bad, but not great.

One other issue is that the laptop seems to be throttled when not plugged in. It seems this occurs at about 20% power. You could hardly hear the fans running and performance took a big hit, with frame drops and eventual full on stuttering after about 50 minutes of play. Still not bad.

Gaming

I was only able to test a couple of games, and they may not bet the typical games that are tested for performance. Nevertheless, the following gives an overview of gaming performance under limited tests.

I began with Sunset Overdrive, which looked great at 4K, 1440P, and 1080P. It struggled to maintain 30 frames per second (FPS) at 4k but performed pretty well at 1440P and 1080P. It felt like a pretty solid 60 FPS at 1080P, but there were some stutters and dropped frames. This game doesn’t have many graphical options.

I also tested some Player Unknowns Battlegrounds at 4K and it seemed fine running at 60FPS with graphics on the highest settings. I was surprised here.

Overall, I’d say the laptop is okay for gaming, but you’re probably best running it at 1080P or setting graphics options to low at 4K. Either way you play, the panel looks great, but is over saturated due to the panel / application issue I noted above.

Photo Editing

With regards to photo editing, I did not encounter any issues using Darktable or Capture One. Adding many modules and edits did not slow the device down and edited photos exported quickly.

Video Encoding

One of the primary reasons for purchasing this laptop was to do video editing in any location. I created some videos with a GoPro Hero 7 and a Fujifilm X-T30, edited them in DaVinci Resolve (color grading, sharpening, LUT), and exported them in 4k MP4. 5 min of 60P footage took about 25 min to export. 5 min of 30P footage took about 15 min to export.

One issue to note is that as you add fusion items and color grading, the playback within DaVinci Resolve can run slowly and scrubbing is choppy. You can solve those issues by changing a few settings within Resolve.

Graphic Design

I created some graphics in Inkscape and GIMP and did not have any issues whatsoever. This laptop works very well with these applications. To be honest, I haven’t thrown anything too difficult at these applications, but for what I’ve used it for (basic graphics, YouTube cover art, featured blog images, bitmap tracing, etc.) there have not been any issues.

Summary

Overall, I am mostly satisfied with the Gigabyte Aero 15. It is a very capable device, with plenty of port options, a beautiful crisp display, and a great form factor. Aside from the Killer Wi-Fi card, the trackpad, and applications not accepting the wide gamut, this device is perfect for my use case.

title: Best value laptop with a few minor gripes and quality control issues.
text:
I got this laptop for Christmas as a gift from my parents since I will be going off to college soon for engineering. I needed a mid-range laptop that had good battery life, solid and light build quality since I will be on the go, a strong CPU and GPU since I will be doing CAD and maybe even some light gaming, and of course a good price. This is a tall order for any laptop but I am impressed with this thin and light.

The 5800u keeps up in demanding CPU tasks when compared to my desktop 3700x that I'm used to and sips on power. I hardly have to bring the power brick with me when I need to use the laptop for light tasks. The 3050 ti is a decent card that gets the CAD work done that I need to at a good pace. Although not anywhere near my desktop 2080 super that I am used to. At the same time the 3050 ti only sips on 40W peak. This is good for battery life but combined with the only 4GB VRAM buffer will hinder gaming performance. Do keep in mind that this is not a gaming laptop and your expectations will be much more realistic. A constant reminder of this is the 60hz screen on the machine. I'm no display reviewer so I will not attempt to expand on the quality of the display, other than that the colors are good enough for me, and while I wish it had a higher refresh rate, the 3050 ti wouldn't be able to make much use of it.

Some of the smaller issues I've had with the laptop are due to the cooling. There are two heat pipes and a fan to cool both the CPU and GPU. This means the laptop can get loud under load and temperatures get a little above my comfort zone after extended periods of time running workloads. The only other criticism I have with the laptop is that the color of the keyboard is light, meaning when the backlight is on in a lit room, it can be hard to see the keys. Couple that with the inconsistent lighting from said backlight and I usually just turn it off.

The last of the negatives I have with this laptop are the quality control issues. I am on my second laptop, which is not an issue I've had with other hardware. I received my first laptop with a trackpad that felt broken on one side. There was also significant backlight bleed on the display to the point where it was obvious even in the windows desktop. I sent it back and the second laptop that I kept solved both of these issues, but the backlight for the space bar is dead. I have decided to just ignore it because I usually turn the backlight off anyway. All of this is to advice that you look at this laptop for defects if you buy it, because there may be some. I could see myself buying Acer products in the future if they are good like this one, but I know to be weary of quality, and you should be too.

This laptop gives impressive specs for the price and a decent build quality, save for the quality control issues and the plastic bezel on the screen. I am able to overlook these things for the value it provides as well as the fact that it masks some of its cost saving with features such as a fingerprint reader and a thin and light body. this is a good laptop if you are willing to make compromises, but that is what you get for searching for high end features on a mid range budget. It is unlikely that a competitor will come out and beat this value, especially considering that the next closest thin and light would likely be HP's line of cheap gaming laptops or one from Asus. Those also wouldn't have the stealthy business look that this does.

As with any expensive product, check out more reviews outside of Amazon, but I do recommend this product if you feel it is right for you.

title: There's some quality control issues
text:
I bought this laptop open box for around $970, definitely not cheap, but a steal for this particular laptop.
The build quality is top notch, screen nice and bright, and just feeling the carbon fiber palm rest is treat by itself.
After the first impressions wore off then came all the problems.
When I reached my car after buying the laptop I opened up the lid to just make sure everything was in order. I put the laptop back in the box and when I got home i discovered that the laptop had been running the whole ride home with the lid closed and was SO SO HOT I COULDN'T EVEN TOUCH IT WITHOUT BURNING MYSELF. It was actually terrifyingly hot. I put the case under my room fan at full speed to cool it down.
Next problem. After using it for about 20 minutes, I found my screen would continuously turn off while I was using it! Like completely turn off as if I was putting it to sleep. After about 8 hours of stress and troubleshooting and countless hours with dell support (to their credit they were very helpful) dell support tells me that there is a setting called "panel self refresh" in the Intel graphics settings that was causing the display to malfunction, and turning the display off. Problem fixed.
NEXT. The thermals. OH THE THERMALS. They are BAD For the processor specifically. It is a very powerful processor. But at stock settings, even opening a few programs at the same time would shoot the processor up to 100 degrees C, making the fans shoot up to maximum speed (quite loud), and the it would thermal throttle relentlessly. I ended up undervolting my processor using a program called throttle stop, and the thermals are better, but this is not something I think the average consumer should have to do to make sure their laptop isn't thermal throttling into oblivion. The GPU (GTX 1650) stays relatively cool (72 C), even under heavy load. No complaints there.
NEXT PROBLEM. The display. There are other versions with IPS panels. I ended up with OLED panel version. It's bright. It's gorgeous. It's 4k. It's almost bezelless. BUT (another BUT), it has noticeable banding with a full grey screen at all brightness levels. It's kinda annoying.
After much research into the problem, I found this OLED panel (made by Samsung) is used in many other pretty high end laptops, and is a widespread issue for all of them. A quick google search for "OLED Banding" confirmed this. It's not just a problem for this laptop either, OLED TV's have this issue as well, so it seems like this is an issue I will just have to live with. The version with the IPS panel does not suffer from this issue.
If you can find this laptop for decent price, sure, it's got some serious value. I wouldn't buy it anywhere near its retail price. Considering the price I got it at ($970), I don't think I'll return it. I'm very savvy with tech and found my way around the issues I've found, other than the OLED panel banding, which is an issue I think I'll live with, but I feel bad for the people who spent full retail price for it and have to deal with the said issues pointed out in my review

title: DO NOT PURCHASE FOR GAMING: Suffers from major ghosting issues
text:
Purchased this monitor to replace my aging Gateway FHD2400 that has began suffering from mura (milky white bars across the screen), and minor burn in. The Gateway monitor was over ten years old (give or take), and aside from a few minor issues was still going strong. It also reacted poorly to lengthy hdmi cables.

I'm happy to say that the Asus monitor does not. However, this monitor is advertised as a 1ms display. I should have done a bit more research on G2G meaning gray to gray. I'm sure it probably does transition from gray to gray at 1ms perfectly fine. When gaming, you are almost never switching from gray to gray. You will be switching from many different colors to many other different colors rather rapidly.

Yes, I have played with all of the settings. For several hours as a matter of fact. Yes I have messed with the trace free setting. I have tried 20, 40, 60, and off. At anything beyond zero, the monitor artifacts badly when anything colored is in motion. You can see horrible blurry after images following behind the moving object. To test for this, set trace free to 60, and scroll up and down on the youtube home screen.

With trace free disabled the ghosting is so bad I can see multiple after images when text is in motion, as if it has become Goku and is leaving multiple copies of its self behind to trick me.

Not only does my ten+ year old Gateway monitor I spent 180 dollars on not suffer from this issue, it has far, far, far, far better color accuracy. There is no way in seven hells that this monitor has a response time of anything less than 10ms when colors are involved, and should be removed from the 1ms category.

It is a decent screen for some light casual gaming, but anything fast paced will cause major eye strain. Especially if you are sensitive to these things. Both the trace free induced color distortion and the ghosting were very noticeable in Dark Souls. If I had a means of capturing the effect on video, I would.

For an inexpensive gaming monitor at 60hz, there are probably better options. I will have to do some extensive research, as it seems this problem has become an accepted norm... which is worrisome.

Unfortunately, I will be returning this display and searching for.. provided I can find one.. a display that does not suffer from noticeable ghosting.

If you are like me, and have an old monitor and an older computer do not give up on your aging friend. Keep that thing, maybe even fix it. Just don't get this monitor thinking that things will improve or that you are actually purchasing a 1ms display on the cheap. As my mom once said 5ms is 5ms. I feel like I would have been better off searching for monitors in that range. At least they are probably not lying about the response time quite so egregiously.

Sorry Asus, I'm a long time supporter of your products. I recommend Asus boards in all of my builds but you really dropped the ball on this one.

title: Great value for the money, just a few cons.
text:
Update 7/14/2022: laptop still works well for my needs. A few new issues lately. The laptop sometimes decides to turn off (not just the screen, the whole thing) if you’re not actively using the mouse. Also when it does this I often have to reconnect to WiFi manually. I’ve tried updating everything and clearing out files but the problem persists. Still not enough to warrant looking for a new one yet.

First off, this laptop looks and feels great and although I haven't had the chance to test many games yet it seems to do well. Since there's plenty of info on the Pros of this laptop (value for the money being a big one) I thought I'd mention a few Cons that really stick out to me.

1) The very first thing I noticed was the power plug-in location. The hole to plug in the power cord is located on the left side of the laptop roughly in the middle. This is a weird location in general but on this laptop it makes even less sense because it means that if you run the cord behind your laptop (like most people) the cord will be directly in front of the fan that blows out the heat from the laptop. This was nearly a deal-breaker for me.

2) This hasn't been an issue yet since I rarely use the laptop unplugged but the laptop boasts 7hrs of battery life unplugged. First off, this doesn't strike me as an impressive stat since my previous laptop was 12hrs. Second; this is only if you don't optimize your settings for gaming. One way the laptop tries to save power is by using the integrated Intel graphics whenever possible. If you tell it to always use the GTX 1060 (as most people will do for gaming) it will be a stronger drain on the battery.

3) The GTX 1060 in this laptop is the Max-Q variant. While this name may make it sound like an upgrade, it is actually slower than the regular 1060. The Max-Q is designed for and used in lighter/thinner laptops but benchmarks show it is roughly 18-20% slower than the base 1060 model. This again might be a deal-breaker for some.

All-in-all this is a great budget gaming laptop and you can't buy a gaming laptop this cheap and expect it to not have a few caveats. However I am considering returning it and spending the extra $200 for something less "limited" for lack of a better word. The 2020 model for $900 seems promising but has the same weird power inlet location.

title: Awesome laptop for the price to performance! Includes FPS for games on 1080p!
text:
Purchased for under $1000 on a promotion on top of a discount code I had. This game plays everything i throw at it. I play 1080p all on maxed settings except AA and shadows. I have AA off and shadows i keep to a medium. It can handle anything 50fps and higher including far cry 4, bf4, bioshock infinite, tome raider and many more new titles. Now that 50 fps minimum is far cry 4 due to being the most demanding game i have. With high/maxed settings i get around 50. Turn off AA and lower shadows and its a nice full 60+ fps the entire time. With AA and shadows on however it realllllllly demands from the GPU making the temps easily hit close to 90^C. By having shadows lowered and AA off, i never seen this laptop get past 83^c which was much better in my opinion. Just because the gpu and CPU can handle that temp doesn't mean the parts AROUND the GPU and CPU can handle those temps. By having these settings turned down it helps keep it cooler and extend the life. The fan gets rather loud but its going too.... its 1 fan cooling an entire laptop. turbo mode helps but a laptop cooler is better Cooler Master has some good 17" laptop coolers that really move air and help. The screen is great quality. The webcam is stunning and the speakers are really awesome. I already voided the warranty by opening the laptop up and installing a 128GB ssd and installed windows 7 on that. kept the 1TB drive for mass storage. BF4 maps load in less than 90 seconds on that HDD which isn't too terrible. My friend's 3.5" drive take him over 3 minutes to load into the same match as me. The brushed aluminum finish makes it have such quality in the build BUT it is SOOOO MUCH a pain to clean. It smudges easy but alcohol wipes do the trick in cleaning it! :)

The batter isn't too bad but PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE UNDERSTAND THIS!

This laptop weighs A LOT! It is not ment to be on your lap, it is a desktop replacement. Gaming battery life on high performance settings wasn't much more than an hour and 40 minutes after a fresh battery calibration using MSI's software.

I highly recommend this laptop but wait for the price to come down. It was listed at $1499 when i bought it in December of 2014. I got it for a steal which is why i got it vs another laptop with better cooling. This laptop is just outright fast and the LED keyboard is awesome!

The DVD drive didn't work but i ordered a replacement one from MSI and amazon credited back the amount back to my method of payment which was nice. I didn't mind installing it myself.

You will need a case to take this around with you...... spend the 20 bucks and get a logic 17.3 inch laptop case. The one i got was model VNCI-217 on amazon.com. Amazing carrying case with VERY good build quality and handle!

title: Great laptop overall
text:

- RBG! The keyboard is RBG backlit as well as the rear exhaust vents. Not everybody will like this feature but for those that do, it’s there! The Alienware software suite also has features to customize the backlighting; colors and patterns.
- RTX2060 gpu. I mean… it beats iGPU hands down!
- The exhaust vents are located on the back, firing outward. This is a good decision in terms of cooling instead of blowing down. Unfortunately, it also leads to a con, the laptops size.
-144Hz panel. I don’t play the type of games where this would have a huge impact but I have noticed that my eyes do feel less “ugh” after gaming sessions.

CONS:

- Size. This thing is a bit on the larger size. Given the cooling design I’m willing to accept it. Not everybody will.
- Heat. This thing does get HOT! Given what it’s got under the hood, I’m not surprised and I’ve become accustomed to this from higher performance/gaming laptops.
- Only has a 500GB Harddrive. It’s a SSD so that’s cool.

Overall, I’m very happy with this laptop. The CONs I listed are mostly nitpicking, None of them are deal breakers and none of them would bring me to return it.

title: Steer Away From Razer! (Read this!)

I would like to start this by saying I've been a brand loyal Razer consumer for years now. After buying my new Razer Blade 15, I have changed my mind. Before you buy this laptop, please read my review. I bought this Razer Laptop a month back. If I had known the issues I would've had with it, I don't think I would've bought it.

It's a $110 charger that has NO fray protection. I have to carry my charger around with me all the time, and only in the last month it's frayed a lot. Did I mention, there are no alternate chargers?
