title: Great all around performer, absolutely beautiful screen
text:
EDIT: In regard to gaming and battery....I played an hour and a half of Untitled Goose Game without the laptop plugged in and then the battery died. For a low graphics game, I'm a bit surprised.

This is a good, balanced, ‘can do a bit of everything’ general use laptop. I know others will go into all the specs and details and what those mean, so I’m going to try and review this for the average person who doesn’t know what all that means.

It’s got a nice look to it. It’s slim, easy to carry, and will fit into any backpack or college class. It looks like a high end machine. Probably the first thing you’re going to notice when you power this up is how great the screen is. It has a 4K UHD display on an OLED screen with Dell’s Infinity Edge. It’s just beautiful. What you want to know from that is that things will look as nice on this screen as they do on your big expensive TV screen. Blacks are dark black, colors are vivid when they ought to be, and soft when they ought to be. The screen goes to the edge of the laptop, and the images nearly to the edge of the screen – there’s a tiny black frame around the edges, but I didn’t notice it…I actually had to boot it up and go look to see if there was any edge at all. Great for watching videos or streaming an online class.

The power cord has a tiny light on the plug where it goes into the laptop. While just a small thing, I find that it’s very useful, especially when travelling, to indicate that I’m actually plugged into a working outlet and not just wasting time hoping it’s charging when it isn’t. Dell put some attention to detail in this. The power cord is a bit over 9 feet long overall. The power brick is 3 feet from the wall plug end. The brick is nice and small; about twice the thickness of a smart phone and similarly sized. Photo is of an LG V30 next to it.

If you’ve never bought a laptop before, and don’t know a lot about computers, this one might seem offputting when you open it – there is the laptop, and the charging cable and brick. There’s a small pamphlet basically telling you to use windows to set it up. For people who like to read the manual first….well, that’s the old way. When you plug it in and turn it on, Cortana, the voice assistant of Windows, welcomes you and tells you what to do. Kind of loudly, to be honest. She can be disabled if you don’t like voice assisted things.

I don’t know if this is usual or if mine was a little wonky to start with. Before Windows 10 home ran it’s necessary updates, I had a lot of problems with whatever was open on the screen going into fits where it would open to full screen and minimize rapidly over and over, and then the whole laptop would shut down. It took a few tries to get the updates downloaded and installed. After that, it seemed to regain it’s sanity. Let it update everything it wants to update.

As usual with any new computer (or even phone) you’ll have to remove a lot of bloatware. This was a pretty quick and easy process. I’m not a fan of McAfee, the virus scan program that’s preloaded onto this laptop, but the first year is free. You can install something else, or put up with it for the first year.

You’ll want to turn off tablet mode. This version does not have a touch screen. What tablet mode does is make your start menu cover the entire display, and you are not able to interact with your desktop. Which is fine if you are on a touch screen device. This particular model is not touchscreen, though I believe it is available as one.

If you need a little more of something, this is fairly easy to upgrade. You have access to the RAM, the battery, the WiFi Card, and the SSD. Don’t forget the screws under the little flap on the bottom.

I like that this has an SD card slot as well as three USB ports (one 2.0, and two 3.0), one is a USB-C, which you can also use to charge your USB-C things. The HDMI port is nice too, and of course, the headphones jack. Having an onboard SD card slot is important to me because I do a lot of photo editing, and it means I won’t have to carry around a card reader as well. Though you do have to be careful as the card sticks out of the slot a bit.

Adding it to my home network was very easy. It picked up the other computers and smart TVs without having to input anything. I can view and interact with pictures stored on my desktop from this laptop just the same as if they were stored right on it, or cast what video I’m watching right to my TV.

I don’t use a computer for gaming that often; mostly for older games. Booting up Mass Effect via Steam, it looked absolutely stunning. I was afraid I’d lose too much detail on the 15.6 inch screen, but I didn’t feel as if I had to strain to see anything. If you are looking for a computer that’s going to be more of a gaming computer than “occasionally, when you travel” this might not work for you, but there are ways to optimize it for gaming, so it’s worth looking up some videos if this is what you want in other respects.

Mainly, I use a desktop, and I like to have my keyboard angled up quite a bit in the back, so going to a laptop’s flat, flush keyboard wasn’t something I was looking forward to. But this isn’t as bad as I thought! The keys have a small amount of click to them – enough that you know when a key has been pressed, but not enough that you’d disturb a lecture while taking notes. And there’s a tactile edge to each key, which I really like. The keyboard is backlit with a subtle blue/white color, not enough to be distracting, but enough that you can easily see what you are doing in a dim or darkened room. The glass touchpad is a nice size, and centered at the bottom of the keyboard. To either side of the touchpad is a lightly textured area, perfect to use as a mousepad.

My only real dislike for this laptop is that it gets really hot. Sitting it on my lap for random internet surfing while watching TV, I had to move it after a while because it got uncomfortably hot. You definitely want one of those heat cushion lap pads for it if you will be using it on your lap or any surface sensitive to heat.

While I did play an hour or so of a game on it, and mostly just used it for videos and internet, I expected it to have more operating noises. I only noticed the fan noise when I was in a quiet room, I was actually worried the fan hadn’t been working. As far as speaker sound, the speakers are in the front bottom, and reflect sound off a hard surface. There are some customization features should you wish to adjust the quality of the sound, but the default is pretty good.

I found that the battery life was about 6 hours of use. Internet, videos, checking messages, writing emails and work stuff…but because the power cord is a decent length, and the brick part of it is smaller than some, it’s not that much of a problem to move it around with you if you need to keep it plugged in for part of the day. It did seem to charge fairly quickly, even during light use.

The camera was nicely responsive in video calls. Sitting in front of a sunny window, the camera kept my face well lit, even when clouds went by and it had to adjust for different lighting. The person on the other end of the call looked clear, and I didn’t experience and lag or artifacts in their image. Sound quality was unremarkable.

TLDR: Good all around performer. Upgradable. Feels nice, looks great, comfortable to use. Some little details really make it nice.

Pictures: 1- Vibrant colors, deep blacks, image nearly to the edge. 2. A light up power plug! 3. About the size of an LG V30.

I got this on a Black Friday sale for just under $900 I believe. So far the overall experience has been basically flawless. Gaming-wise; Hunt: Showdown runs on high settings around 100-120 FPS consistently (and that game is slightly unoptimized), CS:GO maxed out completely.

title: Ideal for work and Gaming
text: The pandemic has forced me to work from home and I have had this laptop for almost a year now. It is great for gaming and day to day functions. I played COD Modern Warfare on it and it runs fine with on normal to slightly high graphic settings.

title: Can run a lot

If there’s any issues it would that sometimes it doesn’t pick up the internets signal which can be a bit annoying but not so much I want to return it, and it’s rather heavy, so traveling with it would probably break your back.

title: Good laptop, has some problems
text:
Let's start with the basics. It's a nice looking laptop. It's a modest looking laptop without much of an obnoxious "gamer" look to it. The build quality on it feels nice and the keyboard is good. It also comes with a little privacy shutter for the camera. The touchpad on it has some issues, which I'll get to later.

I initially bought this laptop for its specs. The i5-9300H that it comes with does quite nicely with a lot of the stuff I work with, especially emulation. It also comes with a GTX 1650, which pairs well. Unfortunately, it only comes with 8GBs of RAM. It only has one RAM slot, which makes upgrade options limited and preventing dual channeling; I only know this from word of mouth, and I can't verify it myself as I don't want to void my warranty by opening my laptop.

Now, onto some minor nitpicks. The screen is a bit dark, although it's not too much of an issue for me. The sound quality on the speakers are decent, but not that great. The battery life is also okay; it gets about five hours with casual usage, and a little under an hour with gaming. The performance on this laptop is also reduced when on battery, so you might as well keep it plugged in when gaming. The F1-F12 buttons have some functions assigned to them (adjusting volume, brightness, etc.), which get in the way sometimes. It's annoying when I try to press Alt-F4 to close a window only to have it mute the microphone instead. Luckily, this can adjusted in the BIOS so that you have to hold the FN button to use these functions (which should've been the default setting in the first place).

Now, onto the biggest issue. The touchpad is absolutely horrible. It's hard to describe, but the momentum on it doesn't feel right. When I try to transition from moving slowly to quickly, the mouse doesn't follow my finger quite right; it's hard to move precisely because of this. I do have a USB mouse on hand, but I honestly prefer to use touchpads, which is why this is such a nuisance for me. It's not even a hardware issue either; it comes from the lack of implementation of Windows's precision touchpad drivers. Lenovo could've issued a simple software update to fix this, but they refuse to do so. If they do fix it, I'd be perfectly willing to up this to a four star review. Bottom line, get a USB mouse if you're going to buy this laptop.

Now, while we're on the subject of purchasing, I believe the original price point for this laptop is somewhere among the lines of $800-900. The specs are great, but I can't recommend it at that price because the design cuts too many corners on a lot of the peripherals (especially the touchpad). It seems like Amazon is selling them for a little under $700, which I suppose is a much more reasonable price.

title: Good performance but serious flaws and reliablity issues
text:
FINAL UPDATE: The laptop has now started spontaneously hard shutting down during gaming. This is my first PC after being a Mac person my whole life, and this quality is dismal and hugely disappointing. I've never had so many problems with a computer.

UPDATE: Downgrading my review by one star; the fan needs replacement on my laptop and dealing with Dell and their contracted technicians has been a disaster. They set up an appointment for me and I stayed home all day waiting for them, losing a day a work, only to have them no show. It's amazing how different dealing with Dell and Apple is, both in service and quality of product.

From a pure spec/preformance standpoint this is a very good laptop. However, there's no such thing as a free lunch; they got these specs at this price point by cutting quite a few corners.

First, the screen is terrible. It's the dimmest screen on any laptop I've ever owned. It's also got lousy field of view.

Second, the thermal handling is abysmal. If you do anything more demanding than writing an e-mail the laptop sounds like a A380 trying to take off above gross weight. Even my kids complain about the noise.

Third, the materials are cheap. Everything is plastic, even the touchpad. The laptop feels flimsy, especially the screen.

Lastly, the Alienware software is unreliable. This is more of an issue with Dell destroying the Alienware franchise, but the included software to control the lighting and thermal settings is barely usable, and needs to be restarted on a regular basis.

Overall, is it a good laptop? Yeah, I'm glad I got it. But it's not nearly the value people think it is relative to something like a Razor. By father got the latter, and I wish I did. For a bit more money, the Razor will have similar performance but will be quiet and give you a phenomenal OLED screen.

title: GREAT value for money!
text:
Incredible value for money! You'll be hard-pressed to find a gaming laptop with these specifications for less than $1800 elsewhere.

Strengths:
Vivid Full-HD display, 144hz refresh rate, great for 4k videos
Excellent graphics (thanks to the RTX2060 GPU)
CPU doesn't break a sweat
Fans not too noisy under regular / non-gaming use
Terrific value at this price from Walmart.com

Weaknesses:
I suspect Acer didn't use the best thermal paste ... CPU & GPU temps are high under load, you can feel the warmth underneath the keyboard. Using a cooling pad somewhat helps during gaming.

Speaking of keyboard, it's not the best, and if you tap it with light keystrokes it'll miss several characters. I've taught myself to bang on the keys a little harder when I type and it seems to be okay, but you'll do yourself a favor by using an external keyboard for typing-intensive tasks.

For audiophiles, the sound quality (from either the built-in speakers or via wired headphones) isn't the best. I recommend disabling Audio Enhancements from the sound settings and then using either a desktop amplifier or an external PC speaker set with its own 3.5mm audio-out port. This way it sounds much cleaner and louder without the silly & over-boosted "enhanced" sound profiles that are all the rage these days.

Lastly, there aren't too many USB ports, so you might need a USB hub, preferably of the powered variety.

For the brave laptop user who's not afraid of opening things up, I would recommend a repaste of the CPU & GPU with Kryonaut Grizzly or Arctic Silver 5 paste to mitigate the high temps. There are several YouTube videos that show how easy it is to open up the unit. However, laptop manufacturers as a whole need to realize the importance of Quality Control and testing in terms of thermal temps and paste-application before their products are boxed and delivered to customers. Take notes, Acer!

If you're going to open it up, you also might as well replace the 802.11ac WiFi adapter with a fairly cheap Intel AX200 802.11AX model, thereby getting WiFi 6 and future-proofing yourself for faster internet that's quickly becoming the norm.

All in all, I do recommend this laptop because you're getting quite a bit of hardware & specs for your money.

title: Great Compromise
text:
I'm a Network/Systems/Infrastructure consultant, and wanted something powerful yet portable to take to client sites, allowing me to run fully virtualized client-server environments. While clearly a mid/upper mid-range gaming rig, the GL502VT-71 fit the bill quite nicely--powerful quad-core i7 6700HQ, 16GB memory, 1TB storage, FHD IPS display, and heck, even a capable GeForce GTX 970m GPU.

The laptop is packaged quite nicely. ASUS clearly put some thought into their design. While the laptop does get quite warm under load, the design of the cooling system keeps components well within their optimal range. I put the system through its paces with some good ole Prime95 stress tests, and the 6700HQ was able to keep things under 80C while still operating in it's Turbo frequency range. Only after I played Forza 6 with Prime95 running in the background did temps ever reach 90C and the CPU operate at its stock/base frequency. Somehow, I was still able to get 50-55FPS out of the game under these conditions. Amazing.

Unfortunately, while the display is quite beautiful most of the time, mine suffers from some terrible backlight bleed/glow in low lit conditions and is most noticeable on dark scenes/images. Its very inconsistent and is worst at the top and bottom bezels. From some quick online research, it seems to be a common issue to ASUS, whether laptop or standalone displays. My display was sourced from Samsung, and apparently has a build date of week 0 year 13. Not sure if accurate or bad EDID info, but I digress.

I am returning it due to the backlight flaws in the display. It's a shame, because I love everything else about this laptop. ASUS did a great job in every other area, but this is one area I can't ignore.

I wanted a replacement but I don't think I wanted to waste my time trying to contact razer since I already knew how bad it was. I just make the charger work until I find a cheaper version perhaps.

Pros:
- Keyboard feels nice (to me atleast) It is really smooth, some people enjoy mechanical keys better but this one is easier for me to manuever around.
- I use this mostly for vrgaming cause my PC is toast so I got this laptop for easier access/transportation (I've played beat saber and vrchat on it for now)
When gaming I always keep the laptop plugged in so I can change my performance in the synapse to custom and I increase the fan speed because the laptop does get pretty hot when gaming. But I also have a cooling device underneath the laptop at all times.
I've also played code vein on this laptop and it runs really good even at Ultra, but it does do a lot of work and I don't really care much for ultra as long as it looks decent.
- You can change the color of the keyboard LED!
- When you get the laptop you should adjust settings to make sure you can make this laptop last long as possible (when I got it, it was always loud sometimes randomly, so I created a custom battery settings and enabled power save mode and battery saver on, this makes the laptop really quiet just for browsing around and my battery always last up to 5 hours compared to when its on high performance I get around 1 hr of battery life)
- No problems so far, and Im hoping I dont come across any (will update review if I do)
- The charger can be plugged into the pc in reverse to if you needed to put in a ethernet cable the charger wont be in the way

Cons:
- Broken charger that came with it
- Mouse is really sensitive so even if you barely touch the touchpad it will click something sometimes
- Heats up hardcore when gaming but thats when you adjust these settings in synapse "while plugged in" settings to custom fan speed to keep it cool. Otherwise I keep synapse off since I've heard it causes problems sometimes.
- Gets super dirty so quick! Especially if you just put lotion on or anything, fingerprints will be everywhere lol! But they provide you with a cloth to get rid of them
- It gets loud when gaming cause of the fan, but thats fair since a small laptop like this is processing so much and I'd rather it get loud and have the fans running so it doesnt overheat.
- It's actually a bit heavy for me, when picking it up and putting it in my backpack but not too much of a complaint
- The battery led on the laptop only shows up when its actually dying or when you put the laptop in hibernate mode. It would be nice sometimes to always see the battery LED because I thought it didnt have one to begin with, but the charger also has a LED light too to let you know its charging.

But thats it, nothing else to add so far. I've adjusted the settings how I wanted it to be. Smooth when not gaming and quiet, enabling battery saver mode and power saver. Fans on high when gaming. I would recommend it but this depends on how much youre willing to gamble, because sometimes you can receive defects and you have to be prepared on taking extra steps.
Also if you do get this, I would install Core Temp. Try to keep the laptop cool while gaming so you dont burn it out so fast :)

title: Would I recommend this computer? I definitely would! but..........
text:
So I've had this laptop for a little over one month and over all I'm happy with my purchase. However, my biggest complaint is how hot it runs when playing games which caused me to give this product 4 stars. I primarily play World of Warcraft and this computer will run it at the highest graphic settings but it gets pretty hot which worries me sometimes and WoW isn't really a super GPU demanding game. You have to prop up the computer on a laptop stand or put a fan underneath it, which is a given for most laptops anyway but you HAVE to do it to help with the temps. I expected it to get hot because it is a super skinny gaming computer but sometimes it'll get up to 170+ degrees Fahrenheit which causes the keyboard to get really hot. With the specs in this computer and for the price, you'd think they would have figured out a better cooling system. I figured out that Google Chrome(which was my primary browser) was a cause to the high temps and switched to Brave which, over all, dropped the temp a little bit. I did a few other things to help manage the temperatures but it still is pretty hot. However, that is my only complaint. The machine runs great, very fast, clean and has a great display. Razer Synapse is also pretty cool. I use it for my Razer Huntsmen Elite keyboard, Razer Basilisk V2 mouse and my Razer Kraken Ultimate headphones. It's really cool looking to have them all glow the same colors with various effects. Also, the materials used on this computer are TOP notch. It looks and feels very Mac like. But it is a finger print magnet causing me to constantly use the microfiber cloth to clean it (OCD habits). You also have the option to add a extra Drive, which I got a 1tb one that I haven't installed yet. As far as battery life, if you are gaming it'll drain the battery pretty fast. I tested it while playing WoW, brightest display, and with a few browser tabs open and it lasted about 3 hours (which doesn't really bother me). The battery life while not gaming and only browsing the web or watching netflix will last about 5-7 hours(give or take)

Would I recommend this computer? I definitely would. I love it. I use this laptop full time over my desktop computer because it is a total beast. I do look forward to future versions of this laptop and hope that they do something about the temperatures.

text:
This is not a high-end "gaming" pc. You will get 5 fps in WZ/MW/BOCW before you even exceed 120 hz output at 1080p. The price you will pay for an actual GPU to see all of the game will cost more than this laptop, so the value is there. It is simply for very low level gaming. Great as a portable dedicated stream rig though.

Valheim hits the wall at 120 hz 1080p. No 4k gaming for this little baby.

The temps will scare you. It does not cool itself. No USB-powered fan will help. You need to buy an appliance cooling unit. It looks like 4 pc fans stuck together with a standard wall outlet. POWER is everything. It needs to plug into the wall, not a measly USB dongle. A wall AC unit helps, but be careful of condensation. (this isn't a joke)

20 mins battery life when gaming--no matter the output.

Your RAM/SSD upgrade will require the cellphone repair kit tools. This baby snaps, which scares the shit out of me. CPU is the bottleneck.

Machine works great!

Please don't buy this with the intention of maxing out settings on modern games. It doesn't work like that. You barely have entry-gaming GPU power with acer helios.

I can take this with me, which is why I bought it. It was wishful thinking to get a gaming rig with 144 hz display for $1200. Hopefully China's ban on crypto mining holds. lol

IF YOU WANT TO PLAY COD, BUY A GPU FIRST AND COLLECT THE REST OF THE BUILD. Don't buy this for gaming. Don't buy this if you think you're getting a 2060 equivalent. It's less gpu than the 1060.

I knew damn well that laptop gpu power is a fraction of desktop, but I thought that jumping to the 3060 would at least let me do 1080p at 144hz.

This isn't a gaming PC.

title: Core Count is not as Advertised, Thermals are Horrendous, GPU/CPU Performance is Bottlenecked
text:
I asked for a return after a few days. This is going to sound like an absolute smear but I genuinely dealt with this.

Update: This laptop has been sitting at the Amazon warehouse since July 31st and I still have not received my refund.

Product is advertised to have 8 core Processor and only has 6 cores. Thermals are bad enough to the point where this laptop can't actually be used on your lap without being burnt (91C on CODMW Min settings). The fan is quite literally the loudest cooling system I have ever heard. My old ASUS ROG G75VW with an i7-3610QM and a GTX 660M GPU is quieter and cooler and I bought it in 2012.

The GPU drivers and bloatware were such a mess even after updating, to where I couldn't even get full use of the 2070 Max Q card. It was running at about 30-40% in tandem with Intel's Integrated Graphics despite me changing multiple times to prefer the 2070 globally in Nvidia's Control Panel.
- This led to lower than should've been FPS in any games I picked up. Overwatch (which is not a demanding game) was struggling to hit 120 FPS on the lowest settings, 50% render scale. (I can hit 150FPS+ on my 3 year old i5-8400 with an AMD RX580 GPU)
- Call of Duty Modern Warfare's performance was worse and I began experiencing thermal throttling.
- Thermal throttling became even worse with the CPU when I moved over to Apex Legends and Titanfall 2, all games with the minimum settings possible.
- I even had FPS issues running Old School Runescape, a 20 year old game you can run on your phone.
- So at that point the 240Hz display became useless because I could not find a game that could sustain 240FPS on this rig.
- One of the darkest displays I've used.
- Sound is pretty low quality, I wouldn't use without headphones. Constant peaks and the bass is too deep/muddy.
- Charging port is in the middle left side of the laptop. Charging cable is pretty short, the brick was dangling off the side of my bed and desk

The only redeeming quality was the weight, it's light. Doesn't really do you any good unless you want to burn your crotch whilst using it on your lap though. The RGB is nice as well if you're into that.

Quite frankly if you're going to dish out $1700 for a laptop, you would at least expect it to be as advertised straight out of the box. It's not worth the hassle for me to work with customer support for multiple weeks/months, and I don't want to play with the refund policy during this pandemic.

Edit: Still waiting on a refund after returning close to 2 months ago. I am still being charged $340 a month for the 5-month financing.

title: For $1100 at the time of purchase - fantastic!
text:
Is it an 85watt Rtx 3070? Yes.
That aside, this thing is fantastic. I use it for hardcore gaming(Tarkov, XCOM 2, Elden Ring, etc). I also use it for my professional work. I have a hub plugged into the USB C with plenty of ports to give me three monitors total as well as more USB 3.1 slots.
The RTX 3070 that is in this thing is no joke. Some people will come in here and claim "well, it might work like such and such card". The 3070 even at 85watts in this laptop performs better than my Windforce x3 2070 that was in my desktop. Not only was there a performance increase in my games but there was a big increase in my lightbaking in Unity and in Blender for those of you that know what that means. Plenty of power in the GPU to play a game in 1080p Ultra and also stream it on Twitch at the same time.
The cpu is also damn good. This laptop replaced a desktop that I had built that had an i5 11400 , 32 gb of 3000 ddr 4, and a rtx 2070. The 11800h outperforms the 11400 desktop CPU in every task I threw at it. I like to mine crypto as a benchmark for testing my equipment(PassMark is also really good - userbenchmarks is a scam - read about it). The 11800h mined at a 30% better rate than the 11400 at a much lower wattage. The RTX 3070 85w that is in the laptop out mined a desktop 2070 at 180w 50mh to 42mh for eth.

The onboard keyboard is responsive and the 144hz screen is just icing on the cake as far as I am concerned. Speakers are good. I use earbuds anyway and this laptop pumps out the volume so you can definitely hear your opponents in games just fine.

Fan control that is on this thing is also great. Sitting here typing this which a few tabs open, discord open, three monitors, and about 10 usb devices plugged in: I am pulling 32c on both the gpu and cpu according to afterburner.

I have been using this machine since Blackfriday 2021. If I had another $110, I would buy it again no question.

title: Runs warm/hot when pushed hard, keyboard backlight is blue only, otherwise awesome!
text:
So coming from console gaming, PC gaming is actually a new experience for me. After a few hiccups I managed to get the Witcher 3, Wild Hunt installed, updated and running with a game pad. I have already played this game on the Nintendo Switch, so I was excited to see what a more robust processor and graphics hardware could do with it.

Well, the graphics are WAY, WAY better than the Switch. I did experience a little hitching in the video very rarely, but I also haven't taken the time to optimize the settings for the hardware (I need to learn how first). Suffice it to say, this game is simply beautiful on this computer. The scenery is gorgeous and it draws you in, in ways that less detailed graphics cannot.

Compared to my aging desktop PC, this machine has probably already saved me a couple of hours over the last week in load times alone. I am an amateur photographer and use Affinity Photo software to process my pictures. This computer opens it within a few seconds, where my older computer used to take at least half a minute. Aside from gaming, photo and video processing are likely to be the most resource-heavy uses I would undertake with this machine, so it's probably going to handle those easily, at least with current generation software.

Waking from sleep mode is lightning fast as well, likely due to the solid state drive. Everything just seems to run smoother.

Like other reviewers, I was a bit surprised at the sheer size of the power supply. It is a monster. Battery life is not great compared to my work laptop, but I imagine most users will have this connected to wall power while gaming anyway. As a substitute for a general purpose computer for typical web browsing and household use, it might be a bit over powered, but it certainly will run common applications fast. These powerful components do tax the battery though, so unless you actually need the power for gaming and other resource hungry apps, you might consider a machine with longer battery life and milder specs.

Things I was a little let down by...

It gets hot and the cooling system runs a little noisy when pushed hard running games. There is enough heat coming out of the vents to make nearby USB and power cables more soft and pliable. I would make sure this has good ventilation all around. I have a separate monitor I like to use, but closing the screen might make cooling more difficult, so keep that in mind.

Also I was surprised to discover it was not a touch screen. There is no fingerprint scanner, and the keyboard backlight is only blue, not RGB. I confirmed this will Dell tech support. They were very helpful and patient, and as with most outsourced tech support, you will have a better experience chatting with them online than talking on the phone. I was really looking forward to the RGB backlight but alas, it wasn't part of this model.

Also, like other reviewers, I noticed the lack of a DVD drive. I ordered one to use installing the game discs.

On to other things, there are 3 total USB ports, one of which is a USB 3.0 and very fast for data transfer. I transferred many, many GB of music to the drive from a big thumb drive and it transferred in less than 20 minutes. The same music files took almost 4 hours to download over my fiber internet connection from Google play.

If you want to use an external monitor, it has an HDMI port for the purpose. I believe it also supports audio over the HDMI protocol so you should be able to game on a flat screen TV just by plugging it in.

There is a 1/8" jack for external speakers or headphones. The on board speakers sounded good listening to several different songs, but are a little underpowered for gaming in a loud family room with dogs barking, kids playing, other entertainment devices going, etc. If this sounds like your house, you will want to connect external speakers.

Styling is nice. The anti-skid feet on the bottom are huge, and it isn't likely to slip on your desk or table if you are a keyboard and mouse gamer. Not sure how you would use a touch pad in that scenario but if you are going to buy a mouse, might as well spend the same money and get a cool looking wireless game pad instead. But again, coming from consoles that's going to be my preference anyway.

So, while it's not a blazing fast, bleeding edge, state of the art gaming machine with all the bells and whistles, it definitely outperforms my Switch by a large margin, and runs other software effortlessly that my older PC often struggles with.

If you are used to using laptop computers costing 1/4 of this one from big retail marts, you will be VERY impressed with its performance. So is it a good value? Given the cost of a current "flagship" cell phone from any of the major brands, I think this is a very reasonable price for a laptop with these specs and capability. It actually costs quite a bit less in today's dollars than a more "cutting edge" laptop I purchased many years ago that would be woefully inadequate to run Windows 10 today. So yes, I think its a good value for the price.

title: Very very good, almost great
text:
There's no denying it that the Blade is a very well-built device. The display isn't premium (not this model anyways), but it's perfectly acceptable. It's great that you can expand the storage and memory, but be aware that the base model only supports up to 32GB (and it must be 2666Mhz).
Overall, the machine seems to perform really well, but there are a couple of power and thermal issues. I managed to get a whopping 25% increase in benchmark score on Cinebench R20 by doing just a couple of really simple things. Firstly, the machine can get rather warm, at which point it will thermal throttle. You can't beat physics, and in this case you've got an all-metal build (metal reflects heat) and it's also very compact (i.e less surface area to spread the heat). So one of the things that really helped a lot was to elevate the laptop. I just placed it on a plastic tray which has a bunch of holes in it, so this gave the fans tons of breathing room. Because of the heat build up, it also means that this laptop will hardly ever be "quiet". The fans are always going...it's not super loud, but definitely noticeable. Perhaps the advanced model with the better cooling architecture would not suffer to quite the same extent. So, lifting the laptop up is one of the big things I did to improve the performance.
The other thing to do is to undervolt the CPU, as this has a dramatically improved the performance. I initially used XTU, but then started using ThrottleStop and got much better results. With the cache undervolted by -0.140 and the core by -0.150 the temperatures dropped a fair margin and there was less power throttling. I also had to enable Speedshift EPP, and this (in combination with the undervolting) finally got the CPU to hit that 4.5GHz speed on single core. Also be sure to put the laptop in "Creator" mode in the Razer settings for best CPU performance.
I could actually get the core undervolted to up to -0.250 which saw a further increase in performance and reduction in temps, but it seems that one of my external hard drives didn't like this and I would get a BSOD. Running on battery also required less of an aggressive undervolt.
Using less power also means longer battery life, and by doing the undervolting I could go from around 2 hours of gaming to 2.5 hours.

Overall, I'm extremely happy with this laptop, and the price of $1099 was incredible. It's very well-built, genuinely feels premium, and the performance met my needs and expectations.

text:
The laptop feels well built and is nice to use physically. It gets most tasks done well enough. The screen looks really good. I like having the extra resolution to see more on the screen when doing spreadsheets and networking work. It has little backlight bleed overall but there is a little around the camera area.

I think the Geforce MX450 in this laptop makes little sense and you’d probably be better off without it. With the native resolution, gaming makes little sense. It is just too much for the MX450. Framerates were all over the place for the most part. I had frequent crashes when gaming too. I am guessing it was heat-related. I was in a 68 F room and the laptop was on a desk and the laptop was super hot. I had a more consistent gaming experience when using a laptop with a Ryzen 5500U and a 1080P screen.

In normal use, like just web browsing the fans are almost always going. They aren’t really annoying but they are audible. If you do any gaming or anything that causes much of a load they will spin up and the laptop will get really hot, concerningly hot which was probably my problem when gaming. I think it is just too much packed into such a small chassis. Again I don’t really think the MX450 has a place here and isn’t helping things.

I was able to plug in the USB C cable from my monitor and get video. The USB devices plugged into the monitor also worked and the monitor would charge the laptop.

I cracked it open and the SSD and Wifi are easily replaceable. I didn’t see any RAM so I am not sure if it is soldered or not. If it isn’t I wasn’t willing to disassemble it any further at this time to see.

So, in the end, it has some nice qualities but everything in it just doesn’t come together well. I wouldn’t recommend this configuration unless you find it at a significant discount and are willing to live with the limitations, knowing that if you push it too hard it will get too hot.

Update 8/6/21: Prior to now I had always been using the computer with the air conditioner on. Today I was using it while the air conditioner was off and immediately noticed the coil wine that the laptop was putting out. If you unplug the power adapter it goes away. So that is annoying.

title: In-Depth Factual Review for Fortnite
text:
Since this is obviously a gaming laptop, and fortnite is a very popular game, I figured I should make an accurate review consisting of details of the laptop‘s performance while running and the pros and cons.
I’ll start with the FPS. You can consistently get 80-130 FPS *DEPENDING ON YOUR GAME’S SETTINGS*
With all settings on Epic, you only get 30-40 FPS. The optimal settings that I have found are as follows:
3D Resolution - 100%
View Distance - Far
Shadows - Off
Anti-Aliasing - Medium
Textures - Medium
Effects - Low
Post Processing - Low
Motion Blur - On

Now when you see “Low” Settings, don’t fear that this will make your game look/perform badly. The game still looks phenomenal on these settings. Using these particular settings you will get 90-130 FPS. I recommend capping your FPS at 120 for optimal performance.

Display
The display is wonderful. It is a very vibrant display and I have no complaints about it.

Input Delay
Now when gaming, having little input delay is essential. This laptop in particular has 2-3ms of input delay, making it a very smooth and responsive experience to play on.

Price
The price for this laptop is crazy. It’s performance exceeds my expectations, especially based on the price.

Also, this laptop can handle streaming if you intend to use it for that.

10/10 would recommend buying this product.

When you get them to reopen the "completed" repair request they will send you another generic email, containing much the same information, plus a few hilarious suggestions that are clearly cut and paste, full of typos, containing illogical suggestions.

The laptop comes with a plethora of bloatware you should remove including wildtangent and several asus related bloatware like live update. I suggest you go to the add / remove programs menu in the control panel and just go to town there using google to figure out what is worth keeping.

In terms of the iffy configuration settings I encountered I noticed that upon checking my computer's properties it looks like the "Allow Remote Desktop" feature came enabled on this laptop. I sure as heck wouldn't have enabled that so it seems like it was just setup that way.

The good:

I've been able to play some of the more recent releases on the highest graphics settings. I followed the other review's suggestion related to the CPU to help with cooling and haven't run into any issues with it getting too hot. I tend to do smaller gaming sessions since I'm a parent so it may just be that I haven't used it consistently enough for long periods to run into that.

The keyboard has a backlight you can turn on/off using the function keys and F3/F4. You can control the sound the same way with F10-F12.

It's a solid gaming laptop and a huge screen and really worth it if you want something that can play newer games at some of the higher settings. The orange cover LED thing is kind of silly but you won't be looking at it most of the time anyhow.

If they'd have ditched the bloatware I'd have given them 5 stars. You should look beyond that though if you need this since you can easily just remove it. Tedious, yes. Terrible, no.

title: Outstanding Profile And Performance Versus Thermals Control
text:
This laptop is elevated by its rubber feet 2 cm off the ground. This really allows more airflow to leave the laptop, which being an AMD system, gets hotter and uses active cooling more aggressively with performance. While this is a laptop that should not be used for long periods of time without an A/C connection, one can actually game at full performance for 4 hours consistently with both fans going at maximum. Thermal throttling takes quite a while (I could only get the 3050 Ti card to throttle after 1.5 hours of Doom Eternal at maximum settings).

In terms of design besides the thermals, the laptop looks like a business class design with a couple of angles. This allows the laptop to fit into standard cases and backpacks.

In terms of modification, this particular model has room for two M2 SSDs (including the SK Hynix supplied 500 GB) and two slots for RAM (2X 8 GB's of Samsung DDR4-3200 included in this laptop). Screw removal and replacement is extremely easy and no further dissembly of the motherboard is necessary to replace the parts.

For someone who wants to game but still needs a laptop for work or light data science matters, the improved thermals and strong balance makes this laptop strongly worth recommending, especially at the price compared with other brands and components. While adding an SSD is a likely upgrade, the included parts are quite good and do not really need to be upgraded in place.

title: A high performance entry without the cost
text:
The Acer Nitro 5 series is perhaps the best general-purpose laptop money can buy – pending that saving money is your objective. I am not much of a techie but when I needed a dedicated windows PC, I had in mind what I needed, and it had to be something that was inexpensive yet built for dedicated processing and upgrade/repairable because I need it to last. I bought this laptop about two years ago and after using it for so long, this has been the most serendipitous purchase I have experienced in a while.

The Acer Nitro 5 is a series of gaming laptops offered in a variety of configurations that varies its graphics card chipset, RAM, and main storage. In my case, I went for the Acer Nitro 5 AN515-51 model which came with a GTX 1050 GPU, 8GB RAM, and 1TB HDD. I will leave it to other reviewers on Amazon and YouTube to tell you about how it plays games because for my purposes, this laptop is overkill. Even at this simple configuration, it can readily handle the most common tasks of an average computer user – from word processing to non-competitive gaming, the hardware can handle it. Speaking of hardware, the Input/output choices are exceptional, featuring both USB-A and one USB-C port with wired ethernet so right out of the box it’s ready to work with almost everything you have without using a dongle. If you can disregard your preconceptions of what a ‘gaming’ laptop and instead look at this as an intermediate-level computer with an emphasis on speed and processing power, the Nitro 5 series is a major step above computers intended for office use.

I am primarily a productivity user and both CPU and GPU have come in great in encoding and decoding files, which is about the only way I can get the fans to be audible. Really, under light usage this laptop is quiet. A backlit keyboard was never a consideration but having worked late into the night, I have come to appreciate just how the red backlights do not interfere with my natural night vision but there is a bit a caveat about its operation. Expectedly, there are power-saving features when this laptop is on battery and one of those is that the backlights will turn themselves off after 30 seconds of inactivity and there is nothing you can do about it. Battery wise, I have averaged about 4 hours with light usage with an average time of 2 hours to fully recharge it. The built-in touchpad quality is poor – or else I have yet to get used to it. I have had incredible experiences with the [[ASIN:B00008XPAR Cirque touchpad]] and drivers and the control are impeccable – the Nitro 5’s touchpad is plasticky and the ‘buttons’ are built-in to the lower part and uses the flex to its advantage. Finally, Bluetooth and USB 3.0 interference are pretty bad. I am not sure if it is my individual laptop [because apparently it is a problem with any computer with both wireless options], but [[ASIN:B003PBZNF8 my wireless mouse]] movement becomes erratic to the point it is unusable. Using the transceiver in the USB 2.0 ports does correct the problem though.

If you have done the search for YouTube, it’s easy to get overwhelmed with the numbers and personalities rating the Nitro 5 but take my word on this – the consensus is that this a good computer for the money. So if the scores and benchmarks mean nothing to you, the Acer Nitro 5 is an inexpensive entry into performance computers without having to eat top ramen longer than anyone should.

title: Very poor performance especially at this high of a price point
text:
[[VIDEOID:570034f0e11ea4920966c4ec2ad9ba94]] I really wanted to like this laptop, I am generally a fan of Razer and have used their products off and on for many years. I was asking for a lot when I decided to purchase this laptop but nothing that wasn’t promised in the Amazon advertising, I was looking for a sleek/quiet/yet powerful laptop that I can use for browsing/gaming. In an attempt to make sure the laptop would be able to handle my requests I even opted for the “advanced” model. This laptop LOOKS great from a physical standpoint and appears quite powerful when it comes to gaming. However, from the first day I tried this laptop I had doubts about whether my purchase was worth it. Even after removing all bloatware and ending all non-essential tasks this laptop IDLES at ~40% memory usage (6-6.5/ 16GB). The laptop is fairly quiet while idle but definitely not silent, and the second any program boots (game/discord/chrome) it will immediately kick in the fans at an obnoxious volume under default razer settings. There are options within razer synapse to manually reduce fan speed which makes the laptop quieter but at the cost of more heat. With the fans on auto (loud) this laptop still generates noticeable heat while idling and over 15-20 minutes reaches near skin-burning temperatures while playing minecraft on the lowest settings, keep in mind this laptop still retails for $2000-2500, that is unacceptable performance for this price point. Additionally, on my second day using this laptop (mind you this is still on default fan settings while playing minecraft on the lowest settings with native resolution) the GPU overheated and crashed the laptop/blackscreened until force shutdown and then needed to wait to cool down before being rebooted. I believe the actual specs of the laptop should be able to handle a heavy workload but the design of this laptop does not supply adequate cooling/heat reduction, especially not without making enough noise to drown out an entire room. Lastly, just a few extra annoyances, the webcam quality is real bad, it looks comparable to my 360p Logitech from the 2000’s. The built-in speakers are laughably awful but that wasn’t a big deal for me as I always use my laptop with headphones. The laptop requires you to not only keep and use the Razer bloatware to customize things like keyboard color/brightness (not super uncommon) but it also must remain running at all times in order to even do things as simple as lower the screen brightness using the function keys. In the end, I may give Razer a try again in the future but I will be taking another deserved break from trying their products after this one.

title: Good Laptop, Short Battery
text:
I've been using this laptop now for four months or so. Here are my thoughts.

For general-use applications, it works very well. I like the size of the keyboard and screen. I like that it comes with a full set of arrow keys. I haven't played too many games, but the ones I have have run very well. For $1,000, the hardware you're getting is very good.

The biggest detractor to the experience has been the battery life, which is almost none at all. Even in full sleep mode, it won't last overnight. You MUST turn the laptop off completely to save battery if you're not going to use it or charge it for a while.

Other than that, with the screen brightness dimmed it has about a 4-5 hour lifespan for doing non-strenuous tasks like word processing. That's okay for me, since I rarely use it without it being plugged in. But if you're looking for a laptop with the virtue of portability and use on the go, this ain't it.

I also have occasional weird audio glitches, but nothing disastrously bad. Just keep it plugged in and you'll have a good time.

title: The Best Gaming Laptop I've Used
text:
As a laptop gamer for the better part of two decades, the rapid progress made in the mobile computing field lately has made me extremely happy. While I normally buy used laptops several years after their release to save on costs, I managed to score a deal on this Blade 15 Base, and I could *not* be happier. It's a massive upgrade over my Blade 14 (2014) in every aspect.

Everything about it screams class, from the aluminum body to the matte black finish. It runs anything you can throw at it, at the full 1080p 144hz with a little tweaking, and it doesn't even break a sweat. Razer finally making user-upgradeable ram slots again is a welcome change from my previous Blade 14 (2014).

The screen resolution, computing power, and thermal envelope all work in balance for once, not pushing too far in any area to sacrifice one of aesthetics, power, or performance. Solid recommend from me.

Pros:
- Runs great. No overheating even under sustained load, stays about 80*C
- Beautiful finish and feel, really is a premium product. No cheap plastic flex!
- User-upgradeable storage and RAM is a big win over previous models.

Cons:
- This is petty AF, but the up-arrow is bumped into the shift row, and it's every bit as annoying as other reviewers say. You get used to it, but man it's irritating.
- The matte black finish, while svelte and premium, does attract fingerprints. You'll get over that, or get a skin, or wipe it down now and then. No big deal.
- Price. I'd argue it's worth it, but my god if you find a sale, snap it up.

title: Gaming Laptop with quite a bit of bloatware and no touchscreen
text:
As per what I've come to expect with Dell hardware, it comes installed with quite a few things I don't really need, however, it definitely does its job for gaming and is decently comfortable for typing as long as you have a laptop desk to protect your lap or use it on a desk.

The orange backlit keyboard is pretty nice for typing (using it to type this review right now) and doesn't feel super mushy like some laptop membrane keyboard, though I'm not yet sure if that'll hold up to long-term hardcore gaming, so even if you're playing at LAN parties elsewhere, I'd probably bring a dedicated keyboard (and of course a mouse) and that brings me to the peripherals.

Basically, this has enough USB ports for a mouse and keyboard and 2 spare ports for other items, or if you happen to use one of the wireless keyboard/mouse combos that use 1 dongle, you'd have 3 available. As well, it does have a standard headphone/mic jack for gaming headset needs along with an ethernet port, and it only has 1 HDMI or you have to use 1 of the USB ports as well for another monitor. I'd say if you're going to use this as your main gaming machine, it would probably be best to invest in a USB dock that can help you solve your port problem, though you'll have to check those specs on them especially since not all of them support high refresh rate gaming, so watch out for that.

Another thing that this does well with is sound quality. I won't say it's super amazing, but you won't be disappointed with the experience, though you'll definitely want a headset when you're not at home with this.

I will also say that this thing gets HOT. Even when it's only using the onboard graphics this thing can kick out heat so be careful when letting it sleep as sometimes it doesn't completely sleep and can get quite hot, so make sure it's well vented when plugged in so you don't have any hot surprises! The brick also cooks as well at times so be careful of that.

Overall, it's a decent gaming laptop, though I'd say it's better as a mobile gaming machine over your main machine, but I'm blessed enough to have a gaming PC that outclasses this laptop but is a royal pain to travel with over this.

title: The Good, The Bad, The Mediocre...
text:
The Good
Weight - Wow, this laptop is light.
Display - I was worried about negative reviews about the gloss and reflectivity, but this hasn't been a problem for me. I think the screen looks great!
TPM - I had no idea this laptop had TPM which is nice because I can encrypt and not have to worry about pre-boot PIN/Passwords.

The Bad
The Arrow Keys - Left and Right are big buttons and Up/Down are little. I never press the correct button. (See picture)
Fingerprint Reader - This is almost worthless. If I am lucky I get a good reading a third of the time. C'mon Acer!!!
Backlit Keyboard - There is no way to control the brightness and the timeout is 30 seconds with no way to keep it on. People on forums have been asking for a BIOS update to address this but still nothing.
Fit and Finish - The casing on the laptop has a lot of imperfections and what I think is overspray. It's weird. (See pictures)

The Mediocre
Battery Life - I thought for sure I would get more! I get about 4 hours in real life.
Function Keys - I expect to be able to swap functionality from function keys to F keys from either software or a key on the keyboard. Nope, not on this laptop - set in the BIOS.
Hyper-Threading - I turn Hyper-threading off on almost every system I use and there is no where in the BIOS to do it. WTF Acer!!!

title: Solid budget gaming laptop with a flew flaws
text:
I had this laptop for the majority of this year before upgrading to a desktop. For the specs, the price was hard to beat with other competitors out there. I chose Nitro for the price to performance and since I also have an aspire that still serves me well. I like the stealth look of the laptop that doesn't make itself too "gamer" like, and the 144hz screen was a surprise considering the price of it! Upgradeability was standard as you can upgrade the RAM and SSD with a 2.5 HDD mounting kit as well. (I added a 1TB HDD and an extra 8GB stick of RAM.)

Games ran like how you'd expect (60+ FPS with mixture of low-med settings) and it does get hot especially with the CPU reaching well into the low 90s° C. It doesn't get uncomfortable when you're playing on the laptop's keyboard near the wasd keys but it was significantly warmer to the left side. I tried repasting the CPU with a much thicker thermal paste but it did not improve temps as much I'd like. There are guides on how to undervolt the laptop to fix the temperatures, but it's not for everyone.

Battery life was bad even for just using it as for browsing and watching videos. I only got around 3-5 hours on a charge even with power saver turned on. So don't try to even game while on battery. Although, charging your phone with the marked USB while the laptop was turned off was a cool feature for it as you can quickly charge up in a pinch.

I did also have some other issues that I encountered, but it's within the OS. For some reason, the built in Audio/Mixer EQ for DTS would sometimes just stop recognizing the speakers and headphones that I plugged in, and I would have to reinstall the OS and force the sound driver to revert to the previous version. Not the end of the world, but it was inconvenient. The most irritating issue I had was when I had an Intel Optane drive plugged in (It does have Optane support since it is an Intel machine) and I would load a game that the Optane drive was on, it would cut all of my USB devices (Mouse, keyboard, and an external drive) for 10-15 seconds before reconnecting. Sometimes it would do it in-game, but most of the time it would cause it when it's mostly using the drive.

Otherwise, this was a solid budget laptop that plays all the modern games without breaking the bank. It has solid features, but with some flaws to get by.

title: Don't buy renewed!
text:
There is a certain degree of trust that Amazon has established with me over the years. I buy products through them with the understanding that not only will the products be of low cost, but will also arrive in a timely manner in working condition.

I've never used the renewed product feature through amazon, but I trusted them and thought I'd give it a try on the MSI GF63 gaming laptop.

The laptop arrived earlier than expected (even during quarantine Amazon managed to work delivery magic.) As I unboxed the product it looked like new. I downloaded steam, epic games, and minecraft to give them a try. Minecraft worked great, subnautica works but it's very touch and go. Then on to Fortnite, this is where i hit a snag.

Fortnite ran fine on ultra settings, but the game itself was unplayable due constant connection issues. I thought perhaps it was just fortnite's servers as my primary desktop worked fine, and my housemates laptop was doing fine. A day later I boot up minecraft to play with my much younger cousin on one of the online servers. And I find myself rubber banding around. This time I'm at his house, and I ask my sister if she's had any network issues. (After running a speed test and trying out several other devices on the wifi I came to the realization that the issue was the wifi card.)

I've spent several hours trying to fix the issue, going through countless forums and trying multiple "guarantee" fixes for this. But at the end of the day, almost every site I checked stated that if nothing else worked, to not rule out that the wifi card has a hardware problem.

So, here I am, with a gaming laptop that, can't game.

title: If you MUST play Windows games, this is a good way to do it.
text:
I'll start off by saying that we're a household who'd pretty much had it with Microsoft, and that this is one of two Windows systems, used pretty much exclusively for gaming. Linux outnumbers Windows in the house, and macOS outnumbers that.

We bought ONE XBOX one and ONE game for it (after eight XBOX 360s, counting RROD replacements, and thousands of games for them, and years and years of Live Gold), and after seeing the garbage UI, and finding that the REMOVED the System Video Player decided we'd had it with the sole remaining product they sold that we'd been buying. Like abandoning Windows, we abandoned XBOX, got a PS4, and every console purchase since had been for that.

As they did with the XP to Vista 'upgrade' (and comparatively Win7 to Windows 'hate\ Windows hate.1'), they took something people liked and replaced it with a steaming dog turd. Win10 is less hideous than hate\hate.1, but nearly every version since around 2003 has been functionally inferior to the version prior. Now, patching problems take systems offline, delete data, or deactivate licenses - It's obvious the company can't manage anything properly anymore and are focused on cramming cloud services down consumers' throats (for profit) rather than fixing the problems they already have.

But the thing is, after years of *nix and Mac game purchases, and Steam game purchases, the problem with Windows-only game availability never really got any better. Console offerings remained comparatively small, bad ports abounded, and on the PC non-Windows availability remained poor. I expected it would, but apparently no-one cares, and the shoddy OS preinstalled on most hardware maintained a near-monopolistic hold. Despite it growing steadily slower, buggier, and uglier.

So eventually, non-Windows remained the 'I care about the experience' platform and for gaming a couple of new Windows systems got added. If you can't live without Windows, the best thing to do is keep it separate from hardware you care about, and away from data you care about. But load it up with Steam games you can't play on Mac or Linux.

The hardware is sleek, and I was unexpectedly happy with the RGB backlit keyboard\lid. I also really liked the lid hinge offset in the middle. I didn't use much of the Asus software aside from a quick walkthrough post-registration, but it's unobtrusive, not annoying, and less unwieldy than Win10 itself. After toggling the 30-or-so privacy toggles from their default 'log everything and send it all to Microsoft' settings, downloading a browser that doesn't suck (two, actually, Firefox AND Chrome), and setting up Steam I was off and running. The display is pretty, if not as pixel-dense as a Retina Mac and all my games looked great on it.

Recent compromised (signed) updater utility issues at Asus aside (and that was a BIG issue, read up on it if it's news o you), the hardware is well designed, the drivers more stable than several other manufacturers' I've used in past, and all-in-all about as good as the Windows experience gets. Would do again, would recommend to others who INSIST on gaming on Windows. If you MUST play Windows games, this is a good way to do it.

title: (Almost) Perfect Portable Gaming machine
text:
Asus has made improvements with every iteration of the Zephyrus, their thin and light gaming laptop. This late 2019 version comes with 16gb Ram, a 15.6" 240hz monitor (1920 x 1080), 1 TB SSD, and the Nvidia RTX 2070 max Q video card.
There is software which switches between the 2070 video card and the onboard Intel graphics card depending if it is needed (you can adjust this with the nvidia controller). You can control the fan speed, lights on the keyboard, etc. with the included software.
You have the option to easily add another 16 mb Ram (32 mb, dual channel) and another ssd card.
Performance is excellent for gaming and you should be able to easily play most games at high refresh rates. However, maximum performance can only be attained by using the ac power adapter and maximizing the cooling of the laptop (fan noise will be high). Due to the very slim and portable design, cooling and fan noise seems to be the most problematic issue with this laptop. There are 3 fan settings, quiet, performance, and turbo. You won't hear much noise at quiet and performance but turbo is definitely noticeable. The fans are quiet at turbo and will automatically go into turbo mode when gaming. If Asus can improve the fan noise and heating issues, this would be the perfect gaming laptop for most people.

Portability, light weight, excellent screen (very bright, clear), Very fast performance for games, good portable desktop replacement
Cons:
Fan noise when gaming, heat

title: Huge improvement
text:
I am comparing this Dell XPS 15 laptop to my Dell Inspiron 15 laptop, and I admit I am blown away. The UHD display is crisp and sharp. Text and graphic detail is amazing. While having the same 15" screen size as my Inspiron, this computer is 3/4" shorter both in width and length. Despite both computers having i7 Intel chips (the Inspiron has 7th Gen, the XPS has 9th Gen) the XPS is, according to PassMark testing, more than 2.6 times faster (5,122 vs 13,620) and it shows. Installs go faster, transfers go faster. Probably the thing that surprised me the most was that the WiFi connection was WAY faster than the Inspiron. Using Speedtest.net and my CenturyLink wifi router the Inspiron had download/upload speeds of 10Mbps/151Mbs. The XPS clocked in as 194/385!! The download speed was almost 20 times faster. Yikes. This wasn't an Ethernet connection, it was WiFi.

Since my most CPU intensive use of this laptop will be music recording, the i7 speed will be very useful as multiple effects on multiple tracks can get pretty CPU intensive. Plus, with an ever growing collection of VST's, the astounding 1Terrabyte SSD drive and 16Megs of memory are ideal. Nice work Dell. XPS does make a difference.

title: The plastic case is GARBAGE
text:
The computer itself is fine. I've had no problems with it running any applications or games. HOWEVER, if you plan on gaming with this computer for any length of time, either you have to have some kind of super-cooler under it or have the fan button turned on to full the entire time, which is as loud as a leaf blower. Otherwise your cheapo plastic case will become as brittle as deadwood and start falling apart one piece at a time until, like mine, the entire corner comes off in your hand. My laptop is now literally held together with duct tape and a prayer. I have to keep it on a wooden board just to hold it together and pray that no more plastic grill pieces end up in the fan blades. The case for this computer is absolutely the worst I have ever seen. I would love to have an aluminum case option, but good luck even finding a plastic replacement case online. A replacement, with labor, will set you back at least 200-400 bucks. For a cheapo plastic case. Expect that cost when you consider buying the extended warrantee. Also, the power brick can get hot enough to cook an egg. Expect it to last about a year.

Good computer when it comes to what matters for gaming and processing. But all the little stuff around it is lowest bidder GARBAGE. Expect damage.

title: Sound issues can be fixed!  A great buy!
text:
I had been contemplating a laptop for quite a while. This is my first as I have always gone the way of desktops until now. With how this computer is equipped, I feel like I got a hell of a deal. Gaming isn't as much of a priority as it had been in the past, but I do some coding and programming that requires some beefy specs. Having a 2.8GHz quad core with 16GB of RAM really makes things easy. And having the SSD makes it boot up in the blink of an eye. And the fans barely make any noise.

The design is great. I love the red accents and backlit keyboard. It's not too cumbersome or too heavy to fit into the laptop pocket of my backpack for traveling.

The only knock that I'm going to give it is what everyone is complaining about. The sound quality! It's awful! They're spotty, they crackle. Doesn't matter what volume level. It always happens.
BUT!!! There is a fix.
I connected headphones expecting for the quality to be better. But it was still bad. That means it's not the speakers. It has to be the sound card or drivers. I tried updating the Realtek drivers since that is the brand, but the update didn't fix it. I instead installed the default Windows drivers, and magically there were no more issues with sound.

Even though I had to play with the drivers to fix the sound, I still consider it to be a solid buy. There is some bloatware that comes with it, but I deleted all of that. Works like a dream!

Ran into a few snags where some things wouldn't work properly by getting the recommended updates from each app (MyAsus, Armory Crate, Windows Update, AMD (Redeon/Adrenalin Edition - Adrenalin edition seems to work better tho it comes with Radeon pre-installed which was causing issues with with a windows update or vice versa). After getting it sorted it all works fine.

My one Con would be no MUX switch but I have bypassed that by using my TV (Samsung not even HDMI 2.1) as a monitor via a USB C to HDMI as a display port. Getting 1440p at 120hz or 4k at 60hz. Also with HDR capabilites tho on windows 11 pro (I opted for free the upgrade) that seems to be buggy. Nothing to do with the computer itself afaik just windows implementation of it. It does work tho, just be sure to get the cords with the right specifications if you want all the bells and whistles your TV or Monitor will support.

title: Great for gaming, but prepare for a hot laptop
text:
This laptop does the job with flying colors, but I wouldn't buy it again.
First of all, games look really good on here. 240hz at 3ms is really impressive for a laptop, and it makes certain games run buttery smooth. The graphics card also makes today's games look really impressive. It's limited to 1080p but I'm able to run most AAA games at high or even ultra with at least 60 FPS. However, running Ray-Tracing with Minecraft showed significant slowdown, especially with a busy screen. If you're into competitive games like League of Legends or Counter-Strike or other games that aren't graphically demanding but demand high frame rates and quick reactions, this laptop is a strong contender.
The biggest problem is that, being an ultra thin laptop, this thing gets hot. I call it "the hot box" because on the most demanding games, certain parts of the laptop get so hot that it hurts to hold your fingers on it. Buying a cooling pad and dusting it out helped it significantly, but even then prepare for above average temperatures. The touch pad is also uncomfortable to use, with my fingers feeling lots of resistance. Despite its light weight and thin profile, taking it around is less viable because the touch pad is so bad. The battery life is also only really good for a few hours at the coffee shop.
I don't regret getting this laptop and it's really useful to me, especially for gaming and other high demand tasks like video editing on the go, but it's uncomfortable to use. It's kind of like a Ferrari, really stylish and good at what it does but not the most practical.

title: Honest review for the GL502VT model
text:
I would like to make a mild PSA before reviewing this. All of the reviews here are for all models of GL502. That means there is a huge discrepancy in power of the machines reviewed as they range from $1200-2500 gaming machines.
My review is for the GL502VT model, the $1200 one with a 1tb hdd, and 970m, and my experience has not involved any heat problems, but tons of issues, errors, and a general disappointment in performance.
I before this was using a touchscreen 2-in-1 dell at the $700 price point which I returned for this, hoping this laptop would better suit my needs. It has not.
I primarily use this laptop for media editing using photoshop, light room, and document processors. I have done less than one hour of gaming on it, on world of warcraft, which was nearly unplayable because apparently the card, nvidia's drivers, the game, and the laptop do not play nicely and the game was extremely unresponsive.

Issues I have had:
The unresponsive game.
Disk use maxing at 100% frequently
Internet connectivity issues
Chrome crashing frequently
Extremely long boot times. As I type this from my phone I am rebooting the computer for the fourth time because it keeps hanging on me instead of starting correctly, and even when it starts correctly it takes forever.
Photoshop apparently cannot use the 970m for acceleration properties. There is some incompatibility and I don't know why.
Photoshop runs slowly as a result.
Random programs become frozen and crash.

There's plenty more but you get the idea. I should have made a detailed list as I noticed them.
All of that said, a lot of my issues were able to be resolved via software updates, system tweaks, property tweaks, changes to settings and services, and maybe some of the ones I am still having could be.
However, this shouldn't be the case. You should not buy a brand new computer over 1k and then do ten hours of problem solving as I definitely have at minimum and still be having issues. You should buy it and it should work. Allowing a company to meet success when they don't fulfill this duty to their best capability is foolish and reinforces bad quality control and piss poor practices.
On top of all of this, it is pretty well none at this point that Asus support not only is terrible, it barely exists. I love Asus for their hardware offerings and build solidity, the only two reasons this is not one star, but this is way over the line.
I am going to purchase a higher up model that has a ssd and a 1000 series card and see if that helps some, but if I start to notice the same problems I'm switching over to MSI.

title: Great performance, poor quality, hideous lights
text:
I’m not a professional gamer, I bought this laptop for high performance gaming on the go. The graphics card is awesome and can handle anything I have thrown at it.

Having said that, I’m really disappointed in the quality of the screen. For $3000 I would expect the screen to be pretty good quality. It’s not an issue with the screen image quality and performance, it’s an issue worth the backlighting. It bleeds through horribly around the edges and in low light it is even more pronounced. The pictures I included are with a black screen saver on. The blotching in the pictures is really only visible in a completely dark room but the bleed out around the edges is worse than you can see in the pictures. During gameplay with bright colors it’s a beautiful screen but when it goes dark it’s just horrible. I wouldn’t want to watch a movie on it. Occasionally I hear a slight whine or buzz from the back edge of the computer and wonder if a capacitor is going to blow on my nearly new computer.

The other issue I have is with the led lighting on the case. Since I travel with this laptop I will occasionally leave it on or in standby/hibernate while plugged in in my room. I have done everything in my power to turn off the LED lighting and everything suggested on forums and the ASUS support site and I still wake up to a damn Las Vegas light show in my room coming from the laptop. Lights are cool but there needs to be an easy way to turn them all completely off. The software has turned off the keyboard and lid lights but the ones around the edges have a mind of their own and it’s annoying as **** to me. The only way I can turn them off is to pull the power from it and shut down or sleep/hibernate so so much for leaving it run while I run an update.

title: One clean machine
text:
I was struggling to find a "classy" gaming laptop that did not look like some 12 year old's toy spaceship, and then came along this Deal of the Day. Now thinking about it, I have literally wasted more money on microtransactions in video games (that 12 year olds play), than I paid for this beautiful and rugged notebook. The construction feels like metal (nice and cool to the touch) and the lighting on the back is also cool. Like the overall design, it is not too flashy but it does stand out from other pleb laptops. I always set my laptops to do nothing when I close the lid, and this also means that you can walk around with the backlight on when the laptop is closed. I think that I might have seen some complaints about the audio, but it sounds great to me. The keys and touchpad are awesome. Low travel on both, and a very convenient fingerprint reader included on the touchpad. I didn't realize how much I would use it. People complain about the webcam, but I like the fact that it has a slide blocker. The positioning seems fine to me also. The real star is the display/graphics here. Compared to all of my other displays, this one stands out clearly because it is so vibrant, details, and easy on the eyes. I have horrible vision so this is a big deal for me. The screen isn't quite matte, but it also is not very reflective so glare is not an issue unless you are outdoors in the sun, maybe. You can easily set the color/brightness of the keys with the included software. My only complaint is the bundled AI widget software. It is not clear what it does, and after researching it I don't think that I want to use it because it regularly reports data from your computer. I removed it and the laptop is running fine, although maybe a bit louder/more fan activity. It is supposed to learn your habits and maximize performance somehow, but I don't buy it.

Update 11/26/21:
This laptop is still holding up really well and it was a great purchase / awesome sale.

title: Fast and Sexy
text:
Excellent laptop. Black, sleek, fast, powerful.

Despite the user comments from back in May, I did my research and bought this machine. I own a Surfacebook III and bought and returned a Legion 7i this year. This AMD-powered Asus Strix Scar has a RTX 3080 GPU and checks all the boxes for a work/gaming hybrid. It has:

1. Speed for days. Loads fast and runs fast and I've been on silent/power-saving mode most of the time!
2. Brilliant display is bright enough, no dead pixels, handles everything I throw at it easily
3. Long battery. I worked unplugged last night for 4 hours and it still showed half a charge left. I was in power saver mode since this thing still runs at 1.6Mhz in that mode.
4. Sexy all black machine with RGB and translucent surface
5. Keyboard has EXCELLENT travel but the click is loud for sure. More importantly, I can type on this for hours very comfortably.
6. VERY VERY good laptop speakers. The 4 speakers have some base and 3D sound. Gets loud with Dolby Atmos enabled.
7. Little things like dedicated volume, mute, play controls; a nice touchpad that doubles as a numpad. You don't notice this stuff until you don't have them (looking at you Legion 7).

It doesn't have
1. A camera
2. A touch screen
3. A smudge-resistant surface

I don't really care one way or the other about their gimmicky keystone attachment or removable corner plate in the rear. I don't use them.

BOTTOM LINE: I've had zero issues and am 10X more satisfied with this machine than I was with the Legion 7. It is black, sexy, fast, fun, cool, and comfy!
