text:
This laptop definitely doesn't as feel as cheap as some other manufactures, and the Razer Blades and MacBooks would always be the gold standard for all laptop design qualities. I'll try and keep this review short and simple.

Pros:
-I like the capabilities of upgrading the components later on in the future if I see it fit.

- Hinge is not as tight as I'd hope.
- The Killer Wifi Card needs to be replaced with something more reliable.
- I wish the 230 Watt power supply would be smaller.
- This is a fingerprint magnet.
- Nose cam shouldn't be a thing.
- The power button wasn't situated properly and was loosened after 9 months in use. (fixed during RMA)
- GPU fan was loose and rattled after 9 months into use. (fixed during RMA)

Overall, I can overlook most of the problems I've had with the laptop. The Gigabyte Support Services (US) is kind and will strive to help resolve your issues. The warranty came in handy when parts needed to be replaced. For the future, I'm just hoping that I won't face any quality control issues again like the fan and power button, but overall a very nice laptop if this wasn't the case.

title: Still great years later and works with Zorin OS / Kubuntu
text:
I used this laptop as my daily work and gaming machine for years. I upgraded the model I bought with a 500 GB SSD and a 1 TB HDD and also increased the RAM to 16 GB. Unfortunately, you can't swap out the GPU or CPU on a laptop, so when the laptop started to slow down and feel a bit dated, I built a new desktop PC for home use.

As far as laptops go, this one is pretty heavy, and I imagine I'll mostly use it when visiting relatives (not carrying around with me day-to-day), but it's a great piece of hardware and I wanted to see what I could do to get more out of it. The most common sense choice was to remove Windows 10 and go with a Linux OS instead.

First I tried Kubuntu, which worked pretty well, but I didn't care for the KDE desktop environment. I use Manjaro Gnome on my desktop, but I wanted something a little different for the laptop, so I went with Zorin OS 16. It installs with no issues and, for the few applications that I use that weren't in their software store (insync for OneDrive syncing was one of them, for example), I just popped open the terminal and took care of that no problem.

And now it runs like it's brand new and looks sharp AF without all the Microsoft spam and branding in the OS. And it runs games that I want to play, although with a few of them it requires a little tinkering, but with the Steam Deck coming out and more games (and EAC and BattlEye) adding Linux support, I can see myself using this laptop for quite a few more years.

title: Quite fast and outstanding, among the best battery life  if you tweak
text:
Battery life

The default battery is good, but if you disable the gpu and drop the cpu power you can get a real 10 hours.
Battery easy to replace, and memory was easy to upgrade, sadly they did solder on one of them. But up to the point they did that you can get dual channel, beyond that single channel. i upgraded to 40mgs

Usage
I got this mainly as a linux development machine, for the keyboard and gpu (when in windows). Keyboard is quite good. it isn't quite lenovo level(nothing is) but pretty close to mac i'd say. I actually prefer it to the m1 since there is more travel, and the quality is fantastic.

Linux
Very good linux support, not quite lenovo level, but honestly it has a new cpu (amd) and a video card, but you can disable it. I went with Manjaro kernel 5.10, for now.There is quite a community that has rallied around asus for Linux so if this is your thing you'll be quite pleased to know it's well supported. Forget about 5.4 for amd, it's all "new" in the linux space. indeed 5.11 is suppose to include more power management for amd and wider compatibility. There are three kernels you need to compile (not this is arch) i assume fedora or ubuntu may not requrie that. but for laptops i like the rolling release of arch/manjaro so i'm not fighting all this built in stuff like nvidia drivers, and such when i want to pull in a new kernel. This is a lot of detail, but kid you not this has good linux support.

Just going to list my cons; leaving it to you to determine impact to you
- keyboard is missing some important keys (pg-up/down begin end) believe it or not. In linux this was a project to fix if you need to, depending on your distribution make some changes with a kernel module. Given my usecase this is the only thing that really disappointed me. But is annoying since there is plenty of space or a simple fn short cut could have done it.
- didn't entirely care for the fact one stick was soldered i find that a stupid apple like move whie i can tolerate that on my mac, i have different expectations in this echosystem.

One other thing worth mentioning is that while the monitor is sharp, it is no apple monitor. i'd have put anther 50 dollars into color reproduction, however i assume for 120hz the options were relatively limited. I put a glass screen protector on it, and it did improve the look. I don't know why i 'm not a physicist but it did.

As a pure gaming computer this is fantastic. The size is so nice. i love having a smaller laptop that is also comfortable to use. I don't entirely understand the big laptop thing

I got some magnetic connectors (10gbs) for my doc where i connect desktop monitors, and swap this with my mac and it works great for that too. Clearly GPU in this computer is a monster, but i also just use display link most of the time since it virtualizes a lot of the gpu bs and sort of standardizes everything, and honestly need a gpu most of the time to scroll though text.

In short this laptop is a great blend of battery life, features, power, and the build quality is fantastic. it's mostly metal. i would have paid more for the bottom to be metal. that part is plastic. I don't love that. But the main body and monitor is metal. Given the cracking issues i have had over the years with other laptops that another win. Again i don't think this is the 90's or even 10 years ago where we were trashing these things every few years. The last one i kept for 10, i assume this one could be even longer.

title: As long as you won't use the keyboard much.....
text:
"The man with a square-wheeled car shall envy his round-wheeling neighbors."

Envy. The designers of this line of laptops and everyone involved in their rollout them should find a new line of work. Not only does form not follow function, some aspects of the form design completely ignore function. Be warned you buy an HP Envy laptop, you will be envying owners of other laptops.

You'll see how they can actually read the keys on their keyboards... while you're stuck with one of the most idiotic design choices I've ever seen make it all the way to retail. GRAY ON SILVER. Snazzy. And it's backlit. But so weak as to only be readable if you're in total darkness. In the twilight zone, the keys appear to be blank--with or without backlighting.

You will need to buy a silicone keyboard cover, affix key stickers--one for each key, or screw it...just grab a sharpie. I tried the silicone cover, but it wasn't for me. The short-throw keys lose tactile feedback. But there are lots of style choices and they are cheap enough. If you didn't heed my advice regarding the laptop, why not try the silicone covers. If you're stuck with an Envy for whatever reason, get the stickers. Mine glow in the dark, which helps me forget about the backlighting that was among my must-have feature requirements.

But that's not all. Unreadable keys, ineffective backlighting, and short-throw keys should be enough to disqualify the Envy from your potential purchase list... you also get a few other "features." The finger reader is not a bonus, so if you don't need it--REALLY need it--skip it. You see, when you gain the finger reader, you lose the right Ctrl key. WHAT?!! There was no where else on the laptop case that they could have put it??! Insert key is just gone. PrtScn is gone, but there's a keyboard combo for that functionality. Who makes these decisions on which keys are unnecessary? The half-height keys, particularly the up and down arrow keys squeezed into a single key space. Look at the keyboard deck. There is vast space available. Couldn't more space been allotted for keys?

Well, if you're the type of person who rests wrists on the aforementioned vast space below the keyboard, you get an exclusive feature. Random key presses occur from time to time if you rest your wrists with too much pressure. And the slick aluminum acts as a heatsink, leeching all the heat from your wrists.

Form took precedent over functionality and usability, affecting aspects of the laptop that you may not include in your comparison checklist when choosing a new laptop. You expect laptop keyboards to suck to some degree, but not to the point of impeding your ability to effectively use the keyboard. And personally, the missing Ctrl key is daily salt in my wound of regret.

You ask, why did I keep the laptop if it's so bad? Sadly, it was a gift that stayed in the box longer than the return window. So stupid. The upside is that the frustration and regret are what motivated me to warn others. Don't let my sacrifice be for naught. DO NOT BUY AN HP ENVY and whatever laptop you are considering, be sure to check all functionality. It might seem silly to verify that a car has round wheels before you purchase it, but that's the level of verification you should use when shopping for a new laptop.

title: Excellent laptop!
text:
9/4/2022: Dell G15 5520 15.6 Inch Gaming Laptop - FHD 120Hz Display, Core i7-12700H, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 512GB SSD, NVIDIA RTX 3060 6GB GDDR6, Intel Wi-Fi 6, Windows 11 - Spector Green

I ordered this to replace my 12 year old desktop computer, which has been showing its age now for quite some time. I never want to sit at a desk anymore anyway, so I've been looking at laptops to replace it for a while now. I've had this one a few weeks now and I am very happy with it so far!

It is very fast and very quiet. I rarely hear the fans at all unless I put my ear right up to it. I have never had a computer this quiet before. It has a nice bright screen, and the keyboard has a numberpad on it! I like the backlit keyboard a lot too.

I don't have any modern PC games at this point (gave up on PC gaming a long time ago since my old desktop couldn't play very many of them) so I can't really review the gaming features yet, but I'm very excited about the opportunity to play games once I get some good ones! It has handled everything else I've tried to do very well - it is faster than my work laptop and MUCH faster than my ancient desktop.

It does eventually get kind of hot on the bottom, enough that it hurts when resting on my legs -- it's still summer so I'm mostly wearing shorts and I have had to put a blanket between the computer and my bare legs. Long pants will solve this problem, but I'm probably going to get some sort of cooling pad anyway so I can be sure it has proper ventilation. It doesn't get hot in the touchpad area on which your hands rest, which is really nice.

It is pretty heavy compared to my 14" work laptop, although I do like the big bright screen a lot. I'm not that strong so this laptop is a lot less portable than a smaller one would be. I can move it from my desk to my couch though, and the big screen is really nice when I'm not near my external monitors.

I have only two (possibly 3?) complaints so far:

1. Very minor complaint with the keyboard layout. They made the arrow keys very short and then put the page up and page down keys just above the left and right arrows.. I'm constantly hitting page up or down when trying to move the cursor left or right. I'm hoping I get used to it. The rest of the keyboard layout is fine, I have no trouble hitting the correct keys aside from the arrow keys.

2. The power cord keeps coming out just enough that the computer won't charge. It looks like it's still in, but then I'll be surprised by a low battery warning. I have to keep pushing it back in to make sure it keeps charging. I don't know if this is an issue with the laptop or with the power adapter, but it doesn't seem like other people are complaining about this very much, so perhaps something is wrong with mine. It doesn't actually have any trouble charging though, just physically keeping the charger plugged in all the way. Not a dealbreaker for me, and I still like the computer just as much.

3. I have not actually tested this yet so I can't say if it's a complaint or not, but according to the specs it appears that the thunderbolt port does not support power delivery, only power share. So I can use my laptop to charge other things, but I can't get a thunderbolt dock that will also charge the laptop. I didn't know anything about thunderbolt ports before so I just assumed they all worked the same way. I can't take off any stars for something that it never promised it could do, and/or for something I can't actually test yet... but if you're looking for a laptop that can be charged by another thunderbolt device, you probably should do a bit more research first. It is very likely this laptop doesn't support that.

Regardless of these complaints, I'm very happy with this laptop! I'd give it 4.5 stars if I could, as 4 stars seems a bit low. I reserve 5 star reviews for when no improvement is necessary though, and I do think the charger or charging port could use some improvement. So, 4 stars it is! I still highly recommend this laptop!

title: Great Specs and Good Looking, but you get what you pay for
text:
For many years I only bought HP machines. This time I needed a machine for media content creation, and HP simply did not offer the display quality, look, or price I wanted. But so far as manufacturing quality, and service levels are concerned, clearly I was spoiled. The quality and performance of all the interior stuff exceeded my expectations. The display is brilliant, the form factor is great too, with a 15.6" display housed in the size of a 14" HP. The speakers, keyboard, etc were all great. In fact on all the big things the machine is great, but it fell apart on the details. The case is cheap, really cheap. Don't expect to ever get it back together perfectly once you crack the case, which you will have to do because of the paltry RAM provided with the machine. There is too much flex in everything, and the first time I cleaned the machine with windex, the finish began to come off.
This really won't pose much of an issue, because with about a one hour battery life, and no upgrade available you will not have to worry about damaging this carrying it anywhere.
The MSI support experience also leaves a lot to be desired. When I called in to complain about the case discoloration. I was told to send it in and wait a couple months for them to get around to working on it. They blamed Covid, of course, but HP would have gotten that fixed in under a week. Updating things like firmware, BIOS, and the components has also proven tough. Since this uses Gen 1 USB-C you will not be able to use a docking station, unless you pop for the MSI one for $300. I have found USB-C performance to be marginal at best. The technology is serveral years old at this point and really shouild have been upgraded.
Forcing the machine to use the GeForce card and skip the integrated Intel graphics has proven nearly impossible for creative content applications. There is an upgrade tool, but its only on the Microsoft Store which of course my new computer could not open.
Recently my web cam stopped working for some mysterious reason, so I just bought an external one. That's how over I am on MSIs support policies.
That being said, so long as I am just working and not trying to transport this, or do anything unusual on it, there is not a single computer in this price range that comes anywhere close to the specs of this one.
MSI is the oppisite of Dell and HP, they do not skimp on the qualty of the components, but everything else they do,
At the end of the day though, I still (six months later) could not buy an HP that does all this does, or a Dell like it for under $3000. So I'm happy. Do not get this if you are a road warrior or to transport back and forth to work, but as a laptop thats sits on your desk, it's perfect. The speed, quality of the screen, and keyboard are really better than anything else you'll find in this price range.

title: Working great so far !
text:
I have not had the laptop long, but so far it is working great. I got this laptop in desperate need of a better one as I had to leave home for an extended period of time, and my old core i5 laptop with it's limited 8gb of memory was killing me.

I needed a laptop with a decent RTX graphics card as I do 3D rendering with my home desktop and I wanted to be sure I got a laptop that would at least let me set the scenes up okay while I am away from home. This laptop does that great, but it does fall behind a bit when it comes to trying to preview the renders or do a full render. Not the fault of the laptop, rendering requires a very beefy GPU, and you can only do so much with a RTX 3060 from a laptop. It's not as good a true RTX 3060 that you use in a desktop.

Anyway, aside from rendering, so far it has worked great for the few games I play. I am not much of a gamer, but I do play several games like Guild Wars 2, Fornite, and a few other Gacha and Idle type games, and they are all working great. Even bench-marking with 3D Mark 11 is giving respectable scores. I did also replace the initial 16GB of memory it came for this [[ASIN:B09S2QLBWC Crucial RAM 64GB Kit]]
with as 16GB just was not enough for a power user like me and the newer memory is faster, but the memory it comes with will be fine for most buyers.

My only complaints so far is similar to what other reviewer have mentioned. The 256Gb SSD it came with is decent and has a okay speed (at a bit over 3000Mbps), but it is just not large enough for my needs, so I ordered a 2Tb replacement drive. Like others mentioned, if you want to install a new SSD, you will need to buy a [[ASIN:B09N7BSPQZ 3rd party bracket and heatsink]] to allow the SSD to be secured down because the existing drive is a 2230 size and the parts it comes with won't be enough to secure a 2280 SSD.

Another complaint is the motherboard and casing of this laptop were clearly designed to hold a second NVME drive, but the board itself does not have the related components built onto it to add one. I just don't get why they did not give us the ability to use that 2nd NVME slot for a slightly higher price. I cannot imagine it would have the manufacturer much to have that 2nd set of parts for another drive and would have greatly increased the value of the laptop. I am forced to use a single 2TB NVME drive installed (supposedly it can support up to 4tb, but was not willing to spend that much), and a combo of a few USB external drives for storage of my 3D assets and all that.

The only other things of note would be the mouse pad can be a little tricky to use (but most will use a external mouse anyway so not a huge thing), and I don't mind the keyboard much, but I do wish the arrow keys were a bit more regular size, but this is a minor annoyance.

If there was one other thing I wish it had, it would be more USB ports. It only has 2 x USB 3.1 ports on the right side, and 1 x Thunderbolt/USB-C and 1 x USB 3.1 port on the back. While this is good for most people, I would have liked to have at least 1 more USB-C port for data use only (since most will use the thunderbolt port for a dock), and/or another USB 3.1 port on the left side of the laptop (which currently has the LAN port and Headphones/Mic port).

Other than 1 BSOD I have gotten so far (GPU related), this laptop is working great nad it not super heavy (which is a big plus for me). I did decide to get a nice little [[ASIN:B09NRTVV3M cooling pad]] for it to assist with keeping it cool while I work on rendering (since it is very CPU and GPU intensive, causing a lot of heat), and while I don't plan to use it on the go much, as many others have pointed out, the battery will not last a super long time.

Most people don't realize just how much power this little laptop needs and the size of the battery just won't allow it to last very long. This is pretty much expected for a gaming laptop. If you want a longer lasting laptop, then you better expect to get a much more expensive laptop (which will also weigh a lot more to accommodate a larger battery), or a less powerful one.

My only real regret is that I did not buy the i9 version with the RTX 3070 Ti GPU since I do use it for rendering. This would have greatly improved my rendering ability, but the extra cost and the fact that I could not get it on the payment plan are the reasons why I did not go that route. If I was not in such a hurry to get it, I would have preferred to get the better model. Maybe some day I can go on eBay and get parts needed to replace the board and CPU to get those specs, but that will be a down the road thing.

title: Makes some compromises; Good, not great, gaming laptop
text:
I've been needing my own laptop for a while now. I have my work PC, but it's nice to have my own system that I can do gaming on without having to worry about questions from IT or my supervisors about what I'm doing instead of the work that I should be doing, so this was a great grab.

The design of this is relatively simple, fitting the design schematics of most modern non-Apple laptops. I am not a huge fan of the color scheme, but it was the only color available when I picked it up, so c'est la vie. Regarding the form factor, I am a fan of the headphone port being on the left side; my work PC has it on the right, which makes it awkward to use on small tables since my mouse often has to cohabitate with the headphone cable (I don't like Bluetooth headphones, so if you do, YMMV). The lack of ad additional HDMI port on the back of the system really marks this as not really intending to be used as part of a flexible desktop dual monitor/portable setup, which contrasts with its relatively high weight (~5.5 lbs) for a machine intended to be carried around or its relatively small screen size. It also has a screen bezel that is, in my opinion, obnoxiously thick. The platform itself is a bit thicker than I like, particularly for systems that I am going to type on regularly. I *think* that this chassis was necessary, however, to accomodate the relatively robust video card that is onboard. And I do say relatively. The 3060 is not a bad card, but it is considerably underpowered compared to the 3070Ti. Perhaps thermals were an issue here, but I suspect the choice of card for this system was based on availability (3060s are supposed to have on-board firmware to limit Ethereum mining, which should make them easier to acquire, even for OEMs), rather than performance. This will probably still run most 2020's era games, but perhaps not at max visual settings; you may get some minor tearing in the vertical if you are running things at their highest levels. The onboard sound is okay and the system speakers are reasonably powerful if you're not wearing headphones, but I'm not sure how often people do that now. If you're going to watch a movie on it, it is probably plenty loud; given the small screen, you won't be sitting that far anyway.

The keyboard is a good size and includes numerics, which means that if I need to do something that is not gaming on this (like prepare my taxes), it should be comfortable to use. Sensitivity across the touchpad is pretty decent.

The battery life is not great, whether doing relatively low-drain things like watching a movie or using more video-card requiring purposes. I was unable to match the claimed battery life; I got about 5-6 hours of use when not running anything intensive. When running something more demanding, it was closer to 3-4.

It comes with Windows 11, which is probably part of the reason the battery life isn't great. You might have better luck if you dual boot into a UNIX-based OS for non-gaming needs. I haven't bothered with that, though, since I usually don't get many opportunities to game for more than an hour or two, and I generally do it from a place where an adapter will work, so it hasn't been a priority for me.

Overall a relatively solid, dependable system. Not great, but sufficient, particularly if you are not interested in a particularly powerful and non-moving desktop setup. The cost is pretty reasonable, given the components. The color isn't my cuppa, but...you get what you get and you don't throw a fit, as they say.

I found that it was due to it running 100% disk all the time which is probably because of a slow HDD.
Now when it comes to gaming, it really sucks. Even when I set my gpu to Nvidia graphics and configured the Nvidia Control Panel, it has a hard time maintaining a steady FPS on CSGO, Fortnite, Apex Legends, R6, etc. Only when I played some really old titles like Mount & Blade Warband, when the laptop worked fine.
Lastly, I think I have a faulty battery because the battery only lasts 1 hr 10 min on a full charge. I've tried to reset the battery and reinstall the driver which shot the battery to 2 hrs, then after 2 days, the battery went back down to 1 hr.

Right now, I always check the task manager to see if my laptop at 100% disk and wait for disk to go down before doing anything. It'll freeze whenever I start going on Google or play my games if I don't wait for the disk to go down.

title: EXACTLY What I Needed...With Extra Goodies
text:
I picked this laptop to replace my MSI Ghost Pro GS60.
Originally bummed about moving from 4K to 1080P, I was quickly distracted by the 144hz refresh rate and just how snappy everything feels on this machine!
Unlike my Ghost Pro, this laptop is likely to never overheat. There are an exorbitant amount of cooling ports and the laptop even has a turbo fan button on the top near the power button! My thermals have yet to go over 84 during stress testing.
MSI is making so many configured laptops you can practically pick and choose what you want now.... that said, this laptop has exactly what I need as a VR gamer, digital product manager, and film maker:
- Great storage (1TB HDD) with a fast SSD for Windows/projects
- Fancy screen with wicked refresh rate for VR video content parity
- IO for VR and future proof USB-C
- Cooling concerns are nonexistant
- 16 jiggly-bits of RAM is more than enough for After Effects/games/Chrome
- Beefy i7 for Adobe Suite
- 1660TI is a GREAT card! Gears 5 at 1440p maxed out, 60+FPS. 120FPS< in VR for games like Beat Saber. Overwatch and CSGO benefit from the 144hz panel/card combo

Wish the battery life was better...90-120 minutes isn't great. Also, this is a THICK laptop, but I don't mind :)
